sentences.zh: 舊唐書　　 卷一百四十一‧列傳第九十一

translations.literal: Old Book of Tang, Volume 141, Biographies 91
translations.idiomatic: Old Book of Tang, Volume 141, Biographies 91

sentences.zh: 田承嗣姪悅　子緒　緒子季安　田弘正子布　牟　布子在宥　張孝忠子茂昭　茂昭子克勤　弟茂宗　茂和　陳楚附

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi; nephew Yue; son Xu; Xu's son Ji'an; Tian Hongzheng's sons Bu, Mou, and Bu's son Zaiyou; Zhang Xiaozhong's son Maozhao; Maozhao's son Keqin; younger brothers Maozong and Maohe; Chen Chu appended
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Tian Chengsi, his nephew Tian Yue, his son Tian Xu and Xu's son Tian Ji'an, Tian Hongzheng and his sons Tian Bu, Tian Mou, and Bu's son Tian Zaiyou, Zhang Xiaozhong and his son Zhang Maozhao, Maozhao's son Zhang Keqin, Zhang's younger brothers Maozong and Maohe, with Chen Chu appended

sentences.zh: 田承嗣，平州人，世事盧龍軍為裨校。

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi was a native of Pingzhou; his family for generations served the Lulong Army as deputy commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi, a native of Pingzhou, came from a family that had served for generations in the Lulong Army as deputy commandants.

sentences.zh: 祖璟、父守義，以豪俠聞於遼、碣。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jing and father Shouyi were famed as bold knights-errant in Liao and Jie.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tian Jing and his father Tian Shouyi were renowned throughout Liao and Jie as men of heroic daring.

sentences.zh: 承嗣，開元末為軍使安祿山前鋒兵馬使，累俘斬奚、契丹功，補左清道府率，遷武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Chensisi, at the end of the Kaiyuan era, served as vanguard military commissioner under Army Commissioner An Lushan; repeatedly captured and killed Xi and Khitan enemies for merit, was appointed Left Qingdao Guard commander, and promoted to Defender-General of the Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Kaiyuan reign, Chengsi served as vanguard military commissioner under An Lushan. He won repeated credit for capturing and killing Xi and Khitan foes, was appointed commander of the Left Qingdao Guard, and was then promoted to Defender-General of the Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 祿山構逆，承嗣與張忠志等為前鋒，陷河洛。

translations.literal: When Lushan plotted rebellion, Chengsi with Zhang Zhizhi and others served as vanguard and seized the He and Luo regions.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, Chengsi marched with Zhang Zhizhi and others in the vanguard and helped overrun the He and Luo heartland.

sentences.zh: 祿山敗，史朝義再陷洛陽，承嗣為前導，偽授魏州刺史。

translations.literal: After Lushan's defeat, Shi Chaoyi again seized Luoyang; Chengsi served as guide and was falsely appointed prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan's fall, Shi Chaoyi seized Luoyang once more. Chengsi led the way and was given the bogus appointment of prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 代宗遣朔方節度使僕固懷恩引迴紇軍討平河朔。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong sent Pugu Huai'en, military commissioner of Shuofang, to lead Uyghur troops to pacify Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong dispatched Pugu Huai'en, military commissioner of Shuofang, to bring Uyghur forces and pacify Hebei.

sentences.zh: 帝以二兇繼亂，郡邑傷殘，務在禁暴戢兵，屢行赦宥，凡為安、史詿誤者，一切不問。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the two rebels had brought successive turmoil and counties and cities were wounded and ruined, aimed to restrain violence and still the armies, repeatedly issued amnesties, and for all misled by An and Shi, inquired into nothing.
translations.idiomatic: With the two rebel regimes having ravaged the realm in succession and the counties left broken, the emperor sought above all to halt violence and quiet the armies. He issued repeated amnesties and would not pursue anyone who had been drawn into the An-Shi cause.

sentences.zh: 時懷恩陰圖不軌，慮賊平寵衰，欲留賊將為援，乃奏承嗣及李懷仙、張忠志、薛嵩等四人分帥河北諸郡，乃以承嗣檢校戶部尚書、鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Huai'en secretly plotted sedition, fearing that when the rebels were pacified his favor would wane, and wishing to keep rebel generals as support; he therefore memorialized that Chengsi, Li Huaixian, Zhang Zhizhi, Xue Song, and four others should each command Hebei prefectures, and Chengsi was made acting Minister of Revenue and prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en meanwhile harbored treacherous designs, fearing that once the rebels were crushed his standing at court would fade. He wanted to keep rebel commanders at hand as allies, and so memorialized that Chengsi, Li Huaixian, Zhang Zhizhi, Xue Song, and three others should each hold command over Hebei prefectures. Chengsi was appointed acting Minister of Revenue and prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄遷魏州刺史、貝博滄瀛等州防禦使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to prefect of Weizhou and defense commissioner of Bei, Bo, Cang, and Ying prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Weizhou and defense commissioner over Bei, Bo, Cang, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 居無何，授魏博節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed military commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he received appointment as military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 承嗣不習教義，沉猜好勇，雖外受朝旨，而陰圖自固，重加稅率，修繕兵甲，計戶口之衆寡，而老弱事耕稼，丁壯從征役，故數年之間，其衆十萬。

translations.literal: Chengsi was unversed in moral teaching, deep-suspicious and fond of valor; though outwardly he received court orders, inwardly he plotted to consolidate himself, heavily increased tax rates, repaired arms and armor, reckoned household numbers, set the old and weak to farming, and the adult males to corvée and campaign service; thus within several years his forces reached one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi had little regard for civil norms. Suspicious by nature and eager for martial glory, he accepted court orders in public while secretly strengthening his own power. He raised taxes sharply, refurbished arms and armor, and tallied households so that the old and weak worked the fields while able-bodied men served on campaign. Within a few years his forces numbered one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 仍選其魁偉強力者萬人以自衛，謂之衙兵。

translations.literal: He also selected ten thousand of the tallest and strongest for his own guard, calling them yamen troops.
translations.idiomatic: He further chose ten thousand of the tallest and strongest men to serve as his personal guard, whom he called the yamen troops.

sentences.zh: 郡邑官吏，皆自署置，戶版不籍於天府，稅賦不入於朝廷，雖曰藩臣，實無臣節。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county officials were all appointed by himself; household registers were not filed with the imperial treasury, and taxes did not enter the court; though called a frontier vassal, in truth he showed no subject's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed all prefectural and county officials himself. Household registers were never sent to the central registers, and taxes never reached the court. Though styled a frontier vassal, in practice he owed the throne no subject's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 代宗以黎元久罹寇虐，姑務優容，累加檢校尚書僕射、太尉、同中書門下平章事，封鴈門郡王，賜實封千戶。

translations.literal: Daizong, because the people had long suffered rebel ravages, for the time being pursued indulgence, repeatedly added acting Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Marshal, and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, enfeoffed him as Prince of Yanmen, and granted a substantive fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Because the common people had suffered so long under the rebels, Daizong chose for the moment to treat Chengsi with forbearance. He repeatedly promoted him—to acting Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Marshal, and Grand Councilor—and enfeoffed him as Prince of Yanmen with a substantive fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及升魏州為大都督府，以承嗣為長史，仍以其子華尚永樂公主，冀以結固其心，庶其悛革；

translations.literal: When Weizhou was raised to a great metropolitan prefecture, Chengsi was made chief administrator; his son Hua was also married to Princess Yongle, hoping thereby to bind his heart and that he might reform.
translations.idiomatic: When Weizhou was elevated to a metropolitan prefecture, Chengsi was made its chief administrator, and his son Hua was married to Princess Yongle in the hope of winning his loyalty and turning him toward reform.

sentences.zh: 而生於朔野，志性兇逆，每王人慰安，言詞不遜。

translations.literal: But born on the northern frontier, his disposition was fierce and rebellious; whenever imperial envoys came to console him, his words were disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Raised on the northern frontier, however, he was by nature violent and defiant. Whenever court envoys came to reassure him, his replies were openly insolent.

sentences.zh: 大曆八年，相衛節度使薛嵩卒，其弟崿欲邀旄節；

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali, Xue Song, military commissioner of Xiangwei, died; his younger brother E wished to seize the command baton.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Dali era, Xue Song, military commissioner of Xiangwei, died, and his younger brother Xue E sought to seize the command.

sentences.zh: 及用李承昭代嵩，衙將裴志清謀亂逐崿，崿率衆歸於承嗣。

translations.literal: When Li Chengzhao was appointed to replace Song, yamen officer Pei Zhiqing plotted disorder to expel E; E led his troops to Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chengzhao was appointed to replace Xue Song, the yamen officer Pei Zhiqing stirred up a mutiny to drive Xue E out, and E led his forces over to Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 十年，薛崿歸朝，承嗣使親黨扇惑相州將吏謀亂，遂將兵襲擊，謬稱救應。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Xue E returned to court; Chengsi sent kin and partisans to incite Xiangzhou officers to plot disorder, then led troops in a surprise attack, falsely claiming relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, after Xue E had submitted to the court, Chengsi sent relatives and clients to stir up the officers of Xiangzhou. He then marched in force on a pretended rescue.

sentences.zh: 代宗遣中使孫知古使魏州宣慰，令各守封疆。

translations.literal: Daizong sent palace envoy Sun Zhigu to Weizhou to proclaim consolation and order each to keep to his borders.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong sent the palace envoy Sun Zhigu to Weizhou with words of reassurance and orders that each commander keep within his own territory.

sentences.zh: 承嗣不奉詔，遣大將盧子期攻洺州，楊光朝攻衛州，殺刺史薛雄，仍逼知古令巡磁、相二州，諷其大將割耳剺面，請承嗣為帥，知古不能詰。

translations.literal: Chengsi did not obey the edict, sent great generals Lu Ziqi to attack Mingzhou and Yang Guangchao to attack Weizhou, killed prefect Xue Xiong, and still compelled Zhigu to tour Ci and Xiang prefectures, hinting that his great generals cut ears and slash faces to ask Chengsi as commander; Zhigu could not interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi refused to obey. He sent Lu Ziqi against Mingzhou and Yang Guangchao against Weizhou, killed the prefect Xue Xiong, and forced Zhigu to tour Ci and Xiang while his officers mutilated themselves and begged that Chengsi be made their commander. Zhigu could not call them to account.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the throne issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 詔下，承嗣懼，而麾下大將，復多攜貳，倉黃失圖，乃遣牙將郝光朝奉表請罪，乞束身歸朝。

translations.literal: When the edict descended, Chengsi was afraid, and among his great generals many again wavered; in panic he lost his plan and sent yamen officer Hao Guangchao to present a memorial asking pardon, begging to bind himself and return to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived, Chengsi was frightened. Many of his senior officers wavered again, and in confusion he lost his bearings. He sent the yamen officer Hao Guangchao with a memorial begging forgiveness and offering to surrender himself to the court.

sentences.zh: 代宗重勞師旅，特恩詔允，并姪悅等悉復舊官，仍詔不須入覲。

translations.literal: Daizong, mindful of the heavy cost in armies, by special grace approved the edict, and nephew Yue and the rest all had their former offices restored; it was further ordered that they need not come to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong, reluctant to weary the armies further, granted the plea as a special favor. Nephew Yue and the others had their former offices restored, and they were told they need not come to court in person.

sentences.zh: 十一年，汴將李靈曜據城叛，詔近鎮加兵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Bian general Li Lingyao seized the city and rebelled; nearby commands were ordered to add troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Bianzhou general Li Lingyao rebelled and held his city. Nearby commands were ordered to raise troops against him.

sentences.zh: 靈曜求援於魏，承嗣令田悅率衆五千赴之，為馬燧、李忠臣逆擊敗之，悅僅而獲免，兵士死者十七八，復詔誅之。

translations.literal: Lingyao sought aid from Wei; Chengsi ordered Tian Yue to lead five thousand men to him; they were met and defeated by Ma Sui and Li Zhongchen; Yue barely escaped, and seven or eight tenths of the soldiers died; an edict again ordered their execution.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyao asked Wei for help, and Chengsi sent Tian Yue with five thousand men. Ma Sui and Li Zhongchen met them and routed the force. Yue barely escaped, and seven or eight soldiers in ten were killed. The court again ordered their punishment.

sentences.zh: 十二年，承嗣復上章請罪，又赦之，復其官爵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Chengsi again submitted a memorial asking pardon; he was again pardoned and his offices and titles restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Chengsi again begged forgiveness in a memorial. He was pardoned once more and had his rank and titles restored.

sentences.zh: 承嗣有貝、博、魏、衛、相、磁、洺等七州，復為七州節度使，於是承嗣弟廷琳及從子悅、承嗣子綰、緒等皆復本官，仍令給事中杜亞宣諭，賜鐵券。

translations.literal: Chengsi held the seven prefectures of Bei, Bo, Wei, Weizhou, Xiang, Ci, and Ming; he was again made military commissioner of the seven prefectures; then Chengsi's younger brother Tinglin, nephew Yue, and sons Wan and Xu all had their former offices restored; Attendant within the Gates Du Ya was still sent to proclaim the order, and an iron certificate was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi held seven prefectures—Bei, Bo, Wei, Weizhou, Xiang, Ci, and Ming—and was again confirmed as their military commissioner. His younger brother Tinglin, his nephew Yue, and his sons Wan and Xu were all restored to office. The Attendant within the Gates Du Ya was sent to announce the court's will, and Chengsi received an iron certificate of mercy.

sentences.zh: 十三年九月，卒，時年七十五。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of the thirteenth year, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 有子十一人：維、朝、華、繹、綸、綰、緒、繪、純、紳、縉等。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons: Wei, Chao, Hua, Yi, Lun, Wan, Xu, Hui, Chun, Shen, Jin, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons: Wei, Chao, Hua, Yi, Lun, Wan, Xu, Hui, Chun, Shen, Jin, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 維為魏州刺史；

translations.literal: Wei was prefect of Weizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Wei served as prefect of Weizhou;

sentences.zh: 朝，神武將軍；

translations.literal: Chao, General of Divine Martiality;
translations.idiomatic: Chao as General of Divine Martiality;

sentences.zh: 華，太常少卿、駙馬都尉，尚永樂公主，再尚新都公主；

translations.literal: Hua, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Commandant of Horse for the Son-in-Law, married Princess Yongle and later Princess Xindu;
translations.idiomatic: Hua as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Commandant of Horse for the Son-in-Law, who married Princess Yongle and later Princess Xindu;

sentences.zh: 餘子皆幼。

translations.literal: the remaining sons were all young.
translations.idiomatic: the other sons were still young.

sentences.zh: 而悅勇冠軍中，承嗣愛其才，及將卒，命悅知軍事，而諸子佐之。

translations.literal: But Yue's valor topped the army; Chengsi loved his talent; when about to die, he ordered Yue to manage military affairs, with the sons assisting.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, however, was the boldest fighter in the army, and Chengsi admired his ability. On his deathbed he put Yue in charge of military affairs, with his sons to assist him.

sentences.zh: 姪 悅悅初為魏博中軍兵馬使、檢校右散騎常侍、魏府左司馬。

translations.literal: Nephew Yue: Yue at first was central-army military commissioner of Weibo, acting Right Regular Attendant, and Left Staff Officer of the Wei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Tian Yue: Yue had first served as military commissioner of the Weibo central army, acting Right Regular Attendant, and Left Staff Officer of the Wei prefectural staff.

sentences.zh: 大曆十三年，承嗣卒，朝廷用悅為節度留後。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dali, Chengsi died; the court appointed Yue military commissioner in temporary charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengsi died in the thirteenth year of Dali, the court named Yue acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 驍勇有膂力，性殘忍好亂，而能外飾行義，傾財散施，人多附之，故得兵柄。

translations.literal: Fierce and brave with great strength, by nature cruel and fond of disorder, yet able outwardly to adorn righteous conduct, pouring out wealth in distribution; many attached to him, and thus he gained military power.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce, strong, and by nature cruel and restless for trouble, yet he could feign righteousness abroad and scatter his wealth freely. Many rallied to him, and so he won control of the army.

sentences.zh: 尋拜檢校工部尚書、御史大夫，充魏博七州節度使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed acting Minister of Works and Censor-in-Chief, and filled the post of military commissioner of the seven Weibo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting Minister of Works and Censor-in-Chief and confirmed as military commissioner of the seven Weibo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大曆末，悅尚恭順。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali, Yue was still deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Through the end of the Dali era Yue still appeared obedient to the court.

sentences.zh: 建中初，黜陟使洪經綸至河北，方聞悅軍七萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, the promotion-and-demotion commissioner Hong Jinglun reached Hebei and only then learned that Yue's army numbered seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era the promotion-and-demotion commissioner Hong Jinglun reached Hebei and learned for the first time that Yue commanded seventy thousand men.

sentences.zh: 經綸素昧時機，先以符停其兵四萬，令歸農畝。

translations.literal: Jinglun had always been blind to the moment; he first issued a tally disbanding forty thousand of his troops and ordering them back to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglun had never understood political timing. He at once issued orders disbanding forty thousand troops and sending them back to farming.

sentences.zh: 悅偽亦順命，即依符罷之，旣而大集所罷將士，激怒之曰：「爾等久在軍戎，各有父母妻子，旣為黜陟使所罷，如何得衣食自資？」

translations.literal: Yue falsely also obeyed the order and at once dismissed them according to the tally; then he greatly gathered the dismissed officers and soldiers and incited them, saying: 'You have long been in the army; each has parents, wives, and children. Now that the promotion-and-demotion commissioner has dismissed you, how can you clothe and feed yourselves?'
translations.idiomatic: Yue pretended to comply and dismissed the men as ordered. Then he assembled the discharged troops and provoked them: 'You have served for years. Each of you has parents, wives, and children. Now that the commissioner has sent you home, how will you live?'

sentences.zh: 衆遂大哭。

translations.literal: The crowd then wept loudly.
translations.idiomatic: The men broke into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 悅乃盡出其家財帛衣服以給之，各令還其部伍，自此魏博感悅而怨朝廷。

translations.literal: Yue then brought out all his household wealth in silks and clothing to give them, ordered each back to his unit, and from this time Weibo was grateful to Yue and resentful of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then distributed his entire household store of silks and clothing among them and sent each man back to his unit. From that day Weibo was devoted to Yue and angry with the court.

sentences.zh: 居無何，或謬稱車駕將東封，而李勉增廣汴州城。

translations.literal: Before long, someone falsely said the imperial carriage would perform the eastern feng sacrifice, while Li Mian enlarged the walls of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward rumors spread that the emperor would perform the eastern feng rite, while Li Mian was enlarging the walls of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 李正己聞而猜懼，以兵萬人屯曹州，遣使說悅，同為拒命。

translations.literal: Li Zhengji heard and grew suspicious and afraid; with ten thousand troops he encamped at Caozhou and sent envoys to persuade Yue to join in refusing orders.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji heard this and grew suspicious and afraid. He posted ten thousand men at Caozhou and sent envoys urging Yue to defy the court together.

sentences.zh: 悅乃與正己、梁崇義等謀各阻兵，以判官王侑、扈萼、許士則為腹心，邢曹俊、孟希祐、李長春、符璘、康愔為爪牙。

translations.literal: Yue then with Zhengji, Liang Chongyi, and others plotted each to hold troops in check; he made staff officers Wang You, Hu E, and Xu Shize his inner circle, and Xing Caojun, Meng Xiyou, Li Changchun, Fu Lin, and Kang Yin his claws and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then joined Zhengji, Liang Chongyi, and others in a plan for each to keep his army in readiness. He relied on the staff officers Wang You, Hu E, and Xu Shize as his inner circle, and on Xing Caojun, Meng Xiyou, Li Changchun, Fu Lin, and Kang Yin as his fighting chiefs.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，鎮州李寶臣卒，子惟岳求襲節鉞，俄而淄青李正己卒，子納亦求節鉞，朝廷皆不允，遂與惟岳、李納同謀叛逆。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, Li Baochen of Zhenzhou died; his son Weiyue sought to inherit the command baton; soon Li Zhengji of Ziqing died, and his son Na also sought the baton; the court refused both, and Yue then joined Weiyue and Li Na in plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong, Li Baochen of Zhenzhou died and his son Li Weiyue asked to succeed him. Soon afterward Li Zhengji of Ziqing died and his son Li Na made the same request. When the court refused both, Yue joined Weiyue and Li Na in plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷遣張孝忠等討恒州，悅將孟希祐率兵五千援之。

translations.literal: At that time the court sent Zhang Xiaozhong and others to attack Hengzhou; Yue's general Meng Xiyou led five thousand men to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: The court then sent Zhang Xiaozhong and others against Hengzhou, and Yue's general Meng Xiyou marched five thousand men to reinforce the rebels.

sentences.zh: 又遣將康愔率兵八千圍邢州，楊朝光五千人營於邯鄲西北盧家砦，絕昭義糧餉之路，悅自將兵甲數萬繼進。

translations.literal: He also sent general Kang Yin with eight thousand to besiege Xingzhou; Yang Chaoguang with five thousand encamped at Lujia Stockade northwest of Handan, cutting the Zhaoyi army's supply route; Yue himself led tens of thousands in armor and followed.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Kang Yin with eight thousand men to besiege Xingzhou and Yang Chaoguang with five thousand to hold Lujia Stockade northwest of Handan, cutting Zhaoyi's supply lines. Yue himself followed with tens of thousands of armored troops.

sentences.zh: 邢州刺史李洪、臨洺將張伾為賊所攻，禦備將竭，詔河東節度使馬燧、河陽李芃與昭義軍討悅。

translations.literal: Xingzhou prefect Li Hong and Linming general Zhang Pi were attacked by the rebels and their defenses nearly exhausted; Ma Sui, military commissioner of Hedong, Li Peng of Heyang, and the Zhaoyi army were ordered to attack Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Xingzhou, Li Hong, and the Linming commander Zhang Pi were hard pressed by the rebels. The court ordered Ma Sui of Hedong, Li Peng of Heyang, and the Zhaoyi forces to campaign against Yue.

sentences.zh: 七月三日，師自壺關東下，收賊盧家砦，大破賊於雙岡，邢州解圍，悅衆遁走，保洹水。

translations.literal: On the third day of the seventh month the army marched east from Huguan, recovered the rebels' Lujia Stockade, greatly defeated the rebels at Shuanggang, relieved the siege of Xingzhou, and Yue's masses fled and held the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the seventh month the imperial army marched east from Huguan, retook Lujia Stockade, and routed the rebels at Shuanggang. The siege of Xingzhou was lifted, and Yue's forces fled to the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 馬燧等三帥距悅軍三十里為壘，李納遣兵八千人助悅。

translations.literal: Ma Sui and the three commanders encamped thirty li from Yue's army; Li Na sent eight thousand men to aid Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui and the other three commanders pitched camp thirty li from Yue's army. Li Na sent eight thousand reinforcements to his aid.

sentences.zh: 魏將邢曹俊者，承嗣之舊將，老而多智，頗知兵法，悅昵於扈萼，以曹俊為貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei general Xing Caojun was Chengsi's old officer, old and full of wisdom, well versed in military law; Yue was intimate with Hu E and made Caojun prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei officer Xing Caojun had been one of Chengsi's veterans—aged, shrewd, and skilled in warfare. Yue favored Hu E instead and relegated Caojun to the prefecture of Bei.

sentences.zh: 及悅拒官軍於臨洺，大為王師所破，悅乃召曹俊而問計焉，曹俊曰：「兵法十倍則攻，尚書以逆犯順，勢且不侔。

translations.literal: When Yue resisted the imperial army at Linming and was greatly defeated by the royal forces, Yue then summoned Caojun to ask his plan; Caojun said: 'In military law, attack when tenfold; the Minister, rebelling against obedience, surely cannot match in strength.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue was badly beaten by the imperial army at Linming, he summoned Caojun for advice. Caojun said: 'The art of war tells us to attack only with tenfold strength. You, Minister, are rebelling against the throne—the odds cannot favor you.

sentences.zh: 宜於口置兵萬人以遏西師，則河北二十四州悉為尚書有矣。

translations.literal: You should place ten thousand men at the mouth to block the western army; then all twenty-four Hebei prefectures would be the Minister's.
translations.idiomatic: Post ten thousand men at the strategic pass to block the western armies, and all twenty-four Hebei prefectures would be yours.

sentences.zh: 今於臨洺、武安設攻城之計，糧竭卒盡，危凶立至，未見其可也。」

translations.literal: Now to set siege plans at Linming and Wu'an—when grain is exhausted and soldiers spent, peril and disaster will come at once; I do not see how this can succeed.'
translations.idiomatic: Instead you lay siege to Linming and Wu'an. When grain runs out and your men are spent, ruin will come at once. I see no wisdom in that.'

sentences.zh: 祐等以其異己，咸譖毀，悅復令守貝州。

translations.literal: You and the others, because he differed from them, all slandered him, and Yue again ordered him to guard Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang You and the others slandered him for dissenting, and Yue again sent him back to guard Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 悅與淄青兵三萬餘人陣於洹水，馬燧等三帥與神策將李晟等來攻，悅之衆復敗，死傷二萬計。

translations.literal: Yue with more than thirty thousand Ziqing troops formed battle lines on the Huan River; Ma Sui and the three commanders with Divine Strategy general Li Sheng and others came to attack; Yue's masses were again defeated, with dead and wounded numbering twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yue drew up more than thirty thousand men from Ziqing on the Huan River. Ma Sui's three armies, with the Divine Strategy general Li Sheng, attacked and routed him again. Some twenty thousand of his men were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 悅收合殘卒奔魏州，至南郭外，大將李長春拒關不內，以俟官軍。

translations.literal: Yue gathered the remnant troops and fled to Weizhou; reaching the outer south gate, great general Li Changchun barred the gate and would not admit him, waiting for the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Yue rallied the survivors and fled to Weizhou. At the outer south gate the general Li Changchun refused him entry, hoping to hold the city for the court.

sentences.zh: 三帥雖進，頓兵於魏州南平邑浮圖，咸遲留不進，長春乃開門內之。

translations.literal: Though the three commanders advanced, they halted the army at the pagoda of Pingyi south of Weizhou, all lingering and not advancing; Changchun then opened the gate and admitted Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The three commanders advanced but halted at the Pingyi pagoda south of Weizhou and lingered without pressing the attack. Changchun then opened the gates and let Yue in.

sentences.zh: 悅持佩刀立於軍門，謂軍士百姓曰：「悅藉伯父餘業，久與卿等同事，今旣敗喪相繼，不敢圖全。

translations.literal: Yue held his girdle sword and stood at the army gate, saying to soldiers and commoners: 'Yue relied on my uncle's remaining enterprise and has long worked with you; now defeat and loss follow in succession, and I dare not seek to preserve myself.
translations.idiomatic: Yue drew his sword and stood at the camp gate, addressing soldiers and townspeople: 'I built on my uncle's legacy and have long shared your fortunes. Now defeat follows defeat, and I no longer dare hope to survive.

sentences.zh: 然悅所以堅拒天誅者，特以淄青、恒冀二大人在日，為悅保薦於先朝，方獲承襲。

translations.literal: Yet the reason Yue firmly resisted heaven's punishment was only that while the two great lords of Ziqing and Hengji lived, they secured recommendation for Yue to the former court, and only then did I obtain succession.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I resisted the court's punishment was that the lords of Ziqing and Hengji, while they lived, secured my succession from the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 今二帥云亡，子弟求襲，悅旣不能報効，以至興師。

translations.literal: Now the two commanders are said dead and their sons and younger brothers seek succession; Yue could not repay the favor, and thus armies were raised.
translations.idiomatic: Now both are dead, and their sons ask to succeed them. I could not repay their kindness, and so war followed.

sentences.zh: 今軍旅敗亡，士民塗炭，此皆悅之罪也。

translations.literal: Now the army is defeated and lost, soldiers and people suffer as if painted in charcoal—all this is Yue's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Our armies are ruined and the people suffer. All of this is my fault.

sentences.zh: 以母親之故，不能自剄，公等當斬悅首以取功勳，無為俱死也！」

translations.literal: For my mother's sake I cannot cut my own throat; you gentlemen should cut off Yue's head to win merit—do not die together!'
translations.idiomatic: For my mother's sake I cannot kill myself. You should cut off my head and win reward from the court—do not die with me!'

sentences.zh: 乃自馬投地，衆皆憐之。

translations.literal: He then threw himself from his horse to the ground, and all pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: He then flung himself from his horse to the ground, and all were moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 或前撫持悅曰「久蒙公恩，不忍聞此！

translations.literal: Someone came forward to support Yue and said: 'We have long received your grace and cannot bear to hear this!
translations.idiomatic: Someone stepped forward to steady him and said: 'We have long owed you our loyalty—we cannot bear to hear this!

sentences.zh: 今士民之衆，猶可一戰，生死以之。」

translations.literal: The soldiers and people today can still fight one battle; we stake life and death on it.'
translations.idiomatic: Our soldiers and people can still fight one more battle. We will live or die together.'

sentences.zh: 悅收涕言曰：「諸公不以悅喪敗，猶願同心，悅縱身死，寧忘厚意於地下乎！」

translations.literal: Yue wiped his tears and said: 'You gentlemen do not despise Yue for defeat, and still wish unity of heart; though Yue die, how could I forget your deep kindness in the underworld!'
translations.idiomatic: Yue wiped away his tears and said: 'You do not abandon me in defeat, and still stand with me. Even in death I shall not forget your loyalty below!'

sentences.zh: 悅乃自割一髻，以為要誓，於是將士自斷其髻，結為兄弟，誓同生死。

translations.literal: Yue then cut off a lock of his own hair as a sworn pledge; thereupon officers and soldiers cut their own hair, bound themselves as brothers, and swore to live and die together.
translations.idiomatic: He cut off a lock of his hair as a sworn pledge. The officers and soldiers cut their hair in turn, bound themselves as brothers, and swore to live and die together.

sentences.zh: 其將符璘、李再春、李瑤、悅從兄昂，相次以郡邑歸國。

translations.literal: His generals Fu Lin, Li Zaichun, Li Yao, and Yue's cousin Ang, one after another surrendered their prefectures and counties to the state.
translations.idiomatic: His generals Fu Lin, Li Zaichun, Li Yao, and his cousin Ang surrendered their districts to the court one after another.

sentences.zh: 璘等家在魏州者，無少長悉為悅所害。

translations.literal: Those of Lin and the others whose families were in Weizhou, young and old alike, were all killed by Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue slaughtered every member of their families still in Weizhou, young and old alike.

sentences.zh: 悅觀城內兵仗罄乏，士衆衰減，甚為惶駭，乃復召邢曹俊與之謀。

translations.literal: Yue saw that within the city arms were exhausted and troops diminished, and was greatly alarmed; he again summoned Xing Caojun to plan with him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the city's arms depleted and its forces dwindling, Yue was terrified and again summoned Xing Caojun for counsel.

sentences.zh: 旣至，完整徒旅，繕修營壁，人心復堅。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he restored the ranks, repaired camps and walls, and hearts were firm again.
translations.idiomatic: When Caojun arrived he reorganized the troops, repaired the walls and camps, and morale hardened again.

sentences.zh: 經旬餘日，馬燧等進至城下。

translations.literal: After more than ten days, Ma Sui and the others advanced to below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days later Ma Sui and the others reached the city.

sentences.zh: 向使燧等乗勝長驅，襲其未備，則魏城屠之久矣，識者痛惜之。

translations.literal: If Ma Sui and the others had ridden victory in a long drive and struck before they were prepared, Weizhou would long ago have been slaughtered; the knowing grieved at this.
translations.idiomatic: Had Ma Sui pressed his victory and struck before the city was ready, Weizhou would have fallen long before. Men of judgment mourned the lost chance.

sentences.zh: 會王武俊殺李惟岳，朱滔攻深州下之，朝廷以武俊為恒州刺史，又以寶臣故將康日知為深趙二州觀察使。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Wujun killed Li Weiyue; Zhu Tao attacked and took Shenzhou; the court made Wujun prefect of Hengzhou and Baochen's former general Kang Rizhi observation commissioner of Shen and Zhao prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: About then Wang Wujun killed Li Weiyue, and Zhu Tao captured Shenzhou. The court made Wujun prefect of Hengzhou and appointed Baochen's former officer Kang Rizhi observation commissioner over Shen and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 是以武俊怨賞功在日知下，朱滔怨不得深州，二將有憾於朝廷。

translations.literal: Therefore Wujun resented that rewards placed Rizhi above him, and Zhu Tao resented not receiving Shenzhou; the two generals bore grievances against the court.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun resented seeing Rizhi rewarded above him, and Zhu Tao resented losing Shenzhou. Both nursed grievances against the court.

sentences.zh: 悅知其可間，遣判官王侑、許士則使於北軍，說朱滔曰：「昨者司徒奉詔征伐，徑趨賊境，旬朔之內，拔束鹿，下深州，惟岳勢蹙，故王大夫獲殄兇渠，皆因司徒勝勢。

translations.literal: Yue knew they could be divided and sent staff officers Wang You and Xu Shize as envoys to the northern army, saying to Zhu Tao: 'Yesterday the Minister received orders to campaign, went straight to the rebel territory, and within a ten-day period took Shulu and reduced Shenzhou; Weiyue's position was tight, so Lord Wang was able to destroy the evil leader—all because of the Minister's victorious momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Yue saw his opening and sent Wang You and Xu Shize to the northern armies with a message for Zhu Tao: 'When you marched under imperial orders, you took Shulu and Shenzhou within a fortnight. Weiyue was cornered, and Wang Wujun could destroy him only because of your victories.

sentences.zh: 又聞司徒離幽州日，有詔得惟岳郡縣，使隷本鎮，今割深州與日知，是國家無信於天下也。

translations.literal: I also heard that on the day the Minister left Youzhou there was an edict granting Weiyue's prefectures and counties to be subordinate to your command; now Shenzhou is cut off and given to Rizhi—this is the state's lack of faith with the world.
translations.idiomatic: When you left Youzhou you were promised Weiyue's districts for your own command. Now Shenzhou is given to Rizhi instead. The court has shown the world that its word cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 且今上英武獨斷，有秦皇、漢武之才，誅夷豪傑，欲掃除河朔，不令子孫嗣襲。

translations.literal: Moreover the present sovereign is heroic and decisive alone, with the talent of Qin Shi Huang and Han Wudi, executing and exterminating bold heroes, wishing to sweep Hebei clean and not allow sons and grandsons to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor is resolute and formidable, with the ambition of the First Emperor and Emperor Wu. He destroys powerful men and means to sweep Hebei clean, leaving no inheritance for our sons.

sentences.zh: 又朝臣立功立事如劉晏輩，皆被屠滅；

translations.literal: Again court ministers who established merit and affairs like Liu Yan and his kind were all slaughtered and destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers who served with distinction, men like Liu Yan, have been destroyed;

sentences.zh: 昨破梁崇義，殺三百餘口，投之漢江，此司徒之所明知也。

translations.literal: yesterday in defeating Liang Chongyi more than three hundred persons were killed and cast into the Han River—this the Minister knows clearly.
translations.idiomatic: when Liang Chongyi was defeated, more than three hundred of his people were killed and thrown into the Han River. You know this well.

sentences.zh: 如馬燧、抱真等破魏博後，朝廷必以儒德大臣以鎮之，則燕、趙之危可翹足而待也。

translations.literal: If after Ma Sui, Bao Zhen, and the others break Weibo the court surely sends cultivated virtuous great ministers to garrison it, then the peril of Yan and Zhao can be awaited by lifting the foot.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ma Sui and Bao Zhen crush Weibo, the court will send civil officials to govern here, and the danger to Yan and Zhao will follow at once.

sentences.zh: 若魏博全，則燕、趙無患，田尚書必以死報恩義。

translations.literal: If Weibo is preserved, then Yan and Zhao have no worry; Minister Tian will surely repay grace and righteousness with death.
translations.idiomatic: If Weibo stands, Yan and Zhao are safe, and Minister Tian will repay you with his life.

sentences.zh: 合從連衡，救災卹患，春秋之義也。

translations.literal: Alliance and linked states, relieving disaster and pitying affliction—this is the meaning of the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: To ally against a common foe and relieve a neighbor's distress is the teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 春秋時諸侯有危者，桓公不能救則耻之。

translations.literal: In Spring and Autumn times when a feudal lord was in peril, if Duke Huan could not save him it was shame.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn era, Duke Huan was shamed if he failed to rescue a lord in peril.

sentences.zh: 今司徒聲振宇宙，雄略命世，救隣之急，非徒立義，且有利也。

translations.literal: Now the Minister's fame shakes heaven and earth, his heroic strategy commands the age; to save a neighbor's urgency is not only to establish righteousness but also profitable.
translations.idiomatic: Your fame fills the realm and your strategy is unmatched. To rescue a neighbor is not only righteous—it is to your advantage.

sentences.zh: 尚書以貝州奉司徒，命某送孔目，惟司徒熟計之。」

translations.literal: The Minister offers Beizhou to the Minister; I am ordered to deliver the accounts—may the Minister consider carefully.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister Tian offers you Beizhou and sends me with the registers. Please weigh this carefully.'

sentences.zh: 滔旣有貳於國，欣然從之，乃命判官王郢與許士則同往恒州說王武俊，仍許還武俊深州。

translations.literal: Tao, already disloyal to the state, gladly followed; he then ordered staff officer Wang Ying and Xu Shize together to go to Hengzhou to persuade Wang Wujun, and still promised to return Shenzhou to Wujun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao, already wavering in loyalty, agreed eagerly. He sent Wang Ying with Xu Shize to Hengzhou to win over Wang Wujun and promised to restore Shenzhou to him.

sentences.zh: 武俊大喜，即令判官王巨源報滔，仍知深州事。

translations.literal: Wujun was greatly pleased and at once ordered staff officer Wang Juyuan to reply to Tao, still managing Shenzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun was delighted and sent his officer Wang Juyuan to answer Zhu Tao, while retaining control of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 武俊又說張孝忠同援悅，孝忠不從，恐為後患，乃遣小校鄭築壘於北境，以拒孝忠；

translations.literal: Wujun also urged Zhang Xiaozhong to aid Yue together; Xiaozhong refused; fearing later trouble, he sent a junior officer Zheng to build a stockade on the northern border to resist Xiaozhong;
translations.idiomatic: Wujun also tried to bring Zhang Xiaozhong into the alliance, but Xiaozhong refused. Fearing him as a future threat, Wujun posted a junior officer named Zheng to build a fort on the northern border against him;

sentences.zh: 仍令其子士真為恒、冀、深三州留後，以兵圍趙州。

translations.literal: and still ordered his son Shizhen as temporary commander of Heng, Ji, and Shen prefectures, with troops besieging Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed his son Shizhen acting commander of Heng, Ji, and Shen while sending troops to besiege Zhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，悅以救軍將至，率其衆出戰於御河之上，大敗而還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, because relief armies were about to arrive, Yue led his masses out to battle on the Imperial River and returned in great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year, expecting relief armies, Yue led his forces out to fight on the Imperial River and was routed.

sentences.zh: 四月，朱滔、武俊蒐軍於寧晉縣，共步騎四萬。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Zhu Tao and Wujun mustered troops at Ningjin County, together forty thousand infantry and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun mustered at Ningjin County a combined force of forty thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 五月十四日，起軍南下，次宗城，滔判官鄭雲逵及弟方逵背滔歸馬燧。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the fifth month they raised the army southward, halted at Zongcheng; Tao's staff officer Zheng Yunkui and younger brother Fangkui deserted Tao and returned to Ma Sui.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the fifth month they marched south and halted at Zongcheng. Zhu Tao's staff officer Zheng Yunkui and his younger brother Fangkui defected to Ma Sui.

sentences.zh: 六月二十八日，滔、武俊之師至魏州，會神策將李懷光軍亦至。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month, Tao's and Wujun's armies reached Weizhou; they happened to meet Shence General Li Huaiguang's army also arriving.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth of the sixth month the forces of Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun reached Weizhou, where they encountered the army of Shence General Li Huaiguang arriving on the scene as well.

sentences.zh: 懷光銳氣不可遏，堅欲與賊戰，遂徑薄朱滔陣，殺千餘人。

translations.literal: Huaiguang's sharp fighting spirit could not be held back; he firmly wished to battle the rebels, so he went straight to press against Zhu Tao's battle line and killed more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang's troops were in such high spirits that none could restrain him; determined to engage the enemy, he drove straight at Zhu Tao's formation and killed more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 王武俊與騎將趙琳、趙萬敵等二千騎橫擊懷光陣，滔軍繼踵而進，禁軍大敗，人相蹈藉，投屍於河三十里，河水為之不流。

translations.literal: Wang Wujun with cavalry generals Zhao Lin, Zhao Wandi, and others with two thousand horsemen struck Huaiguang's formation horizontally; Tao's army pressed close behind and advanced; the imperial army suffered a great defeat, men trampling one another, corpses cast into the river for thirty li, and the river water for this reason did not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun, with the cavalry commanders Zhao Lin and Zhao Wandi and two thousand horsemen, swung into Huaiguang's flank while Zhu Tao's troops pressed on from behind. The imperial army was routed; men crushed each other underfoot, and dead bodies piled in the river for thirty li until the water could scarcely run.

sentences.zh: 馬燧等收軍保壘。

translations.literal: Ma Sui and the others gathered the army and secured the fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui and his fellow commanders pulled their forces back behind their ramparts.

sentences.zh: 是夜，王武俊決河水入王莽故河，欲隔官軍，水已深三尺，糧餉路絕。

translations.literal: That night Wang Wujun breached the river's waters into Wang Mang's old river channel, intending to cut off the imperial army; the water was already three chi deep, and the supply routes were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: That night Wang Wujun diverted the river into Wang Mang's old channel to isolate the imperial troops. The water stood three feet deep, and all supply lines were severed.

sentences.zh: 王師計無從出，乃遣人告朱滔曰：「鄙夫輒不自量，與諸人合戰。

translations.literal: The imperial army had no plan to escape, so they sent men to tell Zhu Tao, saying: "This lowly fellow rashly did not measure himself and joined battle with you all.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial commanders saw no way out and sent an envoy to Zhu Tao with a message: "We overreached ourselves in offering battle to you all.

sentences.zh: 王大夫善戰，天下無敵，司徒五郎與王君圖之，放老夫歸鎮，必得聞奏，以河北之事委五郎。」

translations.literal: Great Doctor Wang is skilled in battle, without peer under Heaven; Minister of Works Fifth Brother and Lord Wang should chart a course—release this old man to return to his province, and we will surely memorialize the throne, entrusting matters in Hebei to Fifth Brother.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wang is invincible in the field; let Minister Tao and Lord Wang work this out among yourselves. Send us back to our posts and we shall report to the throne, leaving Hebei affairs in your hands, Fifth Brother.

sentences.zh: 時武俊戰勝，滔心忌之，即曰：「大夫二兄敗官軍，馬司徒卑屈若此，不宜迫人於險也。」

translations.literal: At that time Wujun had won the battle; Tao bore jealousy in his heart and immediately said: "Great Doctor, you two brothers defeated the imperial army; Minister of Works Ma has humbled himself so—one should not drive men into a corner."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao, already jealous of Wang Wujun's victory, replied at once: "Commander, you and your brother have crushed the imperial army. Minister Ma has abased himself enough—let us not push a foe to the wall."

sentences.zh: 武俊曰：「燧等連兵十萬，皆是國之名臣，一戰而北，貽國之耻，不知此等何面見天子耶！

translations.literal: Wujun said: "Sui and the others field a combined army of one hundred thousand—all are famed ministers of the state. Defeated in a single battle, they bring shame upon the nation; I do not know with what face such men could meet the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun answered: "Sui and the rest command a hundred thousand men, every one a renowned servant of the realm. One defeat has disgraced the dynasty—how can they ever look the Son of Heaven in the face?

sentences.zh: 然吾不惜放還，但不行五十里，必反相拒。」

translations.literal: Yet I do not begrudge releasing them—but if they march less than fifty li, they will surely turn and resist again.
translations.idiomatic: I am willing to let them go—but if you release them before they have marched fifty li, they will turn and fight again.

sentences.zh: 燧等至魏縣，軍於河西，武俊等三將壁於河東，兩軍相持，自七月至十月，勝負未決。

translations.literal: Sui and the others reached Weixian and encamped west of the river; the three generals Wujun and company walled themselves east of the river; the two armies faced each other in stalemate from the seventh month to the tenth, victor undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui and his allies encamped at Weixian on the river's west bank, while Wang Wujun and the other two rebel generals fortified the east. From the seventh month through the tenth neither side could claim the upper hand.

sentences.zh: 悅感朱滔救助，欲推為盟主。

translations.literal: Yue was grateful to Zhu Tao for his rescue and wished to install him as league leader.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by Zhu Tao's aid in his hour of need, Tian Yue sought to make him chief of their alliance.

sentences.zh: 滔判官李子牟、武俊判官鄭儒等議曰：「古有戰國連衡誓約以抗秦，請依周末七雄故事，並建國號為諸侯，用國家正朔，今年號不可改也。」

translations.literal: Tao's aide Li Zimu, Wujun's aide Zheng Ru, and others deliberated, saying: "Antiquity had the Warring States' horizontal alliance sworn to resist Qin; we ask to follow the tale of the seven hegemons at the end of the Zhou, each establishing a state title as feudal lord, adopting the state's calendar and reign era—this year's era name may not be altered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao's staff officer Li Zimu and Wang Wujun's staff officer Zheng Ru proposed: "In the Warring States age the six states joined in alliance against Qin. Let us revive that precedent: each shall proclaim himself a feudal prince under his own title, yet still observe the court calendar and reign title—we need not change the current era name.

sentences.zh: 於是朱滔稱冀王，悅稱魏王，武俊稱趙王，又請李納稱齊王。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhu Tao styled himself Prince of Ji, Yue styled himself Prince of Wei, Wujun styled himself Prince of Zhao, and they also invited Li Na to style himself Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao took the title Prince of Ji, Tian Yue Prince of Wei, Wang Wujun Prince of Zhao, and Li Na was invited to become Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 十一月一日，築壇於魏縣中，告天受之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month they erected an altar in the middle of Weixian and announced to Heaven to receive the titles.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the eleventh month they raised an altar in Weixian and received their titles with rites before Heaven.

sentences.zh: 滔為盟主，稱孤；

translations.literal: Tao as league leader called himself Gu;
translations.idiomatic: As head of the alliance, Zhu Tao styled himself gu.

sentences.zh: 武俊、悅、納稱寡人。

translations.literal: Wujun, Yue, and Na called themselves Gua ren.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun, Tian Yue, and Li Na styled themselves gua ren.

sentences.zh: 滔以幽州為范陽府，恒州為真定府，魏州為大名府，鄆州為東平府，皆以長子為元帥。

translations.literal: Tao made Youzhou into Fanyang Prefecture, Hengzhou into Zhending Prefecture, Weizhou into Daming Prefecture, and Yanzhou into Dongping Prefecture, in each case appointing his eldest sons as marshals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao renamed Youzhou Fanyang Prefecture, Hengzhou Zhending, Weizhou Daming, and Yanzhou Dongping, placing an eldest son at the head of each.

sentences.zh: 偽冊之日，其軍上有雲物稍異，馬燧等望而笑曰：「此雲無知，乃為賊瑞。」

translations.literal: On the day of their false investiture, above their army cloud patterns were slightly unusual; Ma Sui and others gazed up and laughed, saying: "These clouds are ignorant—serving as an omen for rebels.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of their bogus enthronement strange clouds gathered above their camp. Ma Sui and his colleagues looked up and laughed: "Clouds have no sense of their own—they take omens for traitors.

sentences.zh: 又其營地前三年土長高三尺餘，魏州戶曹韋稔為土長頌曰：「益土之兆也。」

translations.literal: Also, three years before at their camp ground the earth had risen more than three chi in height; Wei Prefecture Registrar Wei Ren composed a eulogy on the earthen mound, saying: "A portent of increased territory."
translations.idiomatic: Three years earlier the ground at their camp had swelled upward more than three feet. Wei Ren, a registrar of Wei Prefecture, praised the mound as an augury of expanding lands."

translations.literal: Such was the text of their prophecy."
translations.idiomatic: So ended their reading of the omen.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，涇師犯闕，諸帥各還本鎮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year, the Jingzhou army violated the capital; the various commanders each returned to their home provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year, when mutinous troops from Jingzhou stormed the capital, every rebel commander pulled back to his own territory.

sentences.zh: 悅、滔、武俊互相疑惑，各去王號，遣使歸國，悅亦致書於抱真，遣使聞奏。

translations.literal: Yue, Tao, and Wujun mutually distrusted one another; each dropped his royal title, sent envoys to submit to the state; Yue also wrote to Bao Zhen and dispatched envoys to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue, Zhu Tao, and Wang Wujun turned suspicious of one another, renounced their royal titles, and sent envoys to renew allegiance to the court. Yue also wrote Li Bao Zhen and dispatched messengers to inform the emperor.

sentences.zh: 興元元年正月，加悅檢校尚書右僕射，封濟陽王，使並如故，仍令給事中、兼御史大夫孔巢父往魏州宣慰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xingyuan, Yue was promoted to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed as Prince of Jiyang, with his commission unchanged; additionally, Palace Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief Kong Chaofu was sent to Weizhou to proclaim consolation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xingyuan 1 the court promoted Tian Yue to acting Right Vice Director of State Affairs, created him Prince of Jiyang, and confirmed his existing posts, while dispatching Palace Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief Kong Chaofu to Weizhou to announce the imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 時悅阻兵四年，身雖驍猛，而性愎無謀，以故頻致破敗，士衆死者十七八。

translations.literal: At that time Yue had held out with arms for four years; though personally fierce and bold, by nature he was obstinate and without strategy, and for this reason repeatedly met defeat; of his troops and masses seven or eight tenths died.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue had defied the court with armed force for four years. Personally fierce in battle, he was stubborn and devoid of strategy, and defeat followed defeat until seven or eight soldiers in ten had perished.

sentences.zh: 魏人苦於兵革，願息肩焉，聞巢父至，莫不舞忭。

translations.literal: The people of Wei suffered under warfare and arms, wishing to lay down their burdens; when they heard Chaofu had arrived, none did not leap and rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei were exhausted by war and longed for peace; when word came that Kong Chaofu was on his way, they rejoiced as if dancing.

sentences.zh: 悅方宴巢父，為其從弟緒所殺。

translations.literal: Yue was just then feasting Chaofu when he was killed by his younger cousin Xu.
translations.idiomatic: While entertaining Kong Chaofu at a banquet, Tian Yue was slain by his cousin Tian Xu.

sentences.zh: 子 緒緒，承嗣第六子。

translations.literal: Son — Xu. Xu was Chengsi's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tian Xu was the sixth son of Tian Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 大曆末，授京兆府參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dali era he was appointed a military aide in the Jingzhao Prefecture government.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Dali period he received an appointment as aide in the Jingzhao prefectural administration.

sentences.zh: 承嗣卒時，緒年幼稚。

translations.literal: When Chengsi died, Xu was still young.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xu was still a child when Tian Chengsi died.

sentences.zh: 承嗣慮諸子不任軍政，以從子悅便弓馬，性狡黠，故任遇之，俾代為帥守。

translations.literal: Chengsi worried that his sons could not manage military and civil affairs; because his nephew Yue was skilled with bow and horse and by nature cunning and clever, he therefore favored and employed him, causing him to replace him as commander and guardian of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that none of his own sons could handle military command, Chengsi turned to his nephew Yue, who was adept at riding and archery and sharp-witted by nature. He entrusted him with power and made him de facto ruler of the province.

sentences.zh: 及緒年長，悅以承嗣委遇之厚，待緒等無間，令主衙軍。

translations.literal: When Xu grew to maturity, Yue, because Chengsi had honored and favored him generously, treated Xu and the others without distinction and had him command the yamen army.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu came of age, Yue— mindful of the great trust Chengsi had placed in him— showed Xu equal favor with his own brothers and put him in charge of the headquarters guard.

sentences.zh: 緒兇險多過，悅不忍，嘗笞而拘之，緒頗怨望，常俟釁隟。

translations.literal: Xu was cruel and dangerous with many faults; Yue could not bear it, once flogged and imprisoned him; Xu held much resentment and constantly waited for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was vicious and unruly, and when Yue could stand it no longer he had him flogged and imprisoned. Xu nursed a grievance and watched continually for his chance.

sentences.zh: 會興元元年，朝廷宥悅，仍令孔巢父往宣慰。

translations.literal: It happened that in the first year of Xingyuan the court pardoned Yue and again ordered Kong Chaofu to go proclaim consolation.
translations.idiomatic: It was the first year of Xingyuan; the throne pardoned Tian Yue and once again sent Kong Chaofu to bring the imperial message of favor.

sentences.zh: 悅旣順命，門階徹警。

translations.literal: Yue having submitted to the edict, guards at the gate and steps were fully withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yue had accepted the court's terms, the guards at his gate were dismissed entirely.

sentences.zh: 悅宴巢父夜歸，緒率左右數十人先殺悅腹心蔡濟、扈萼、許士則等，挺劒而入。

translations.literal: Yue feasted Chaofu and Chaofu returned at night; Xu led several dozen attendants, first killing Yue's trusted men Cai Ji, Hu E, Xu Shize, and others, then drawing swords and entering.
translations.idiomatic: After the banquet Tian Yue saw Kong Chaofu home at night. Xu led a few dozen followers, cut down Yue's closest advisers—Cai Ji, Hu E, and Xu Shize— and stormed inside sword in hand.

sentences.zh: 其兩弟止之，緒斬止者，遂徑升堂。

translations.literal: His two younger brothers tried to stop him; Xu killed those who stopped him, then went straight up to the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Two younger brothers tried to halt him; Xu killed them on the spot and marched straight into the main hall.

sentences.zh: 悅方沉醉，緒手刃悅并悅妻高氏，又入別院殺悅母馬氏。

translations.literal: Yue was just then deep in drunkenness; Xu personally blade-killed Yue together with Yue's wife Lady Gao, then entered a separate courtyard and killed Yue's mother Lady Ma.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue was dead drunk. Xu ran him through with his own hand, killed Yue's wife Lady Gao, then entered the side courtyard and murdered his mother Lady Ma.

sentences.zh: 自河北諸盜殘害骨肉，無酷於緒者。

translations.literal: Since the various bandits of Hebei had ravaged their own flesh and blood, none was crueler than Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the Hebei warlords who butchered their own kin, none matched Xu's brutality.

sentences.zh: 緒懼衆不附，奔出北門，邢曹俊、孟希祐等領徒數百追及之，遙呼之曰「節度使須郎君為之，他人固不可也。」

translations.literal: Xu feared the masses would not attach to him, fled out the north gate; Xing Caojun, Meng Xiyou, and others led several hundred followers, overtook him, and called from afar, saying, "The military commissioner must be done by the young lord—others simply cannot do it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, fearing the troops would not follow him, fled through the north gate. Xing Caojun, Meng Xiyou, and several hundred men caught up with him and shouted from a distance: "Only you, sir, can command this army—no one else will do.

sentences.zh: 乃以緒歸衙，推為留後。

translations.literal: They then brought Xu back to headquarters and installed him as acting military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: They escorted Xu back to headquarters and proclaimed him acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明日，歸罪於扈萼，以其首徇，然後稟於孔巢父，遣使以聞。

translations.literal: The next day they assigned blame to Hu E, displayed his head as warning, then reported to Kong Chaofu and sent envoys to inform the court.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they pinned the crime on Hu E, paraded his head as a warning, reported the matter to Kong Chaofu, and sent messengers to notify the court.

sentences.zh: 時緒兄綸居長，為亂兵所殺，遂以緒為留後。

translations.literal: At that time Xu's elder brother Lun was senior in age and was killed by mutinous soldiers; thereupon Xu was made acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's eldest brother Lun, who stood first in line, had been killed in the mutiny, so Xu was confirmed as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 朝廷授緒銀青光祿大夫、魏州大都督府長史、兼御史大夫、魏博節度使。

translations.literal: The court appointed Xu Silver Blue-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, chief administrator of the Weizhou metropolitan prefecture, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Weibo Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court invested Xu as Silver Blue-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, chief administrator of Weizhou, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Weibo military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時朱滔率兵兼引迴紇之衆南侵，緒遣兵助王武俊、李抱真，大破朱滔于經城，以功授檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Tao led troops and also brought Uyghur forces south in invasion; Xu dispatched troops to aid Wang Wujun and Li Bao Zhen, greatly defeating Zhu Tao at Jingcheng; for merit he was appointed Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao marched south with Uyghur allies, Xu sent troops to support Wang Wujun and Li Bao Zhen and routed Zhu Tao at Jingcheng. For this victory he was made acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，以嘉誠公主出降緒，加駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, Princess Jiacheng was sent out to marry Xu; he was additionally made Captain of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 Princess Jiacheng was given to him in marriage, and he received the post of Captain of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 尋遷檢校左僕射，封常山郡王，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan Commandery, with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to acting Left Vice Director of State Affairs, created Prince of Changshan with an estate of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 改封鴈門郡王，食實封五百戶。

translations.literal: His title was changed to Prince of Yanmen Commandery, with a substantive fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Prince of Yanmen with a substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋加同平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Co-Equal to the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 初，田悅性儉嗇，衣服飲食，皆有節度，而緒等兄弟，心常不足。

translations.literal: Initially, Tian Yue's nature was frugal and stingy; clothing and food and drink all had regulation, but Xu and the other brothers' hearts were constantly dissatisfied.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Tian Yue lived frugally, regulating every garment and meal, yet Xu and his brothers were never content.

sentences.zh: 緒旣得志，頗縱豪侈，酒色無度。

translations.literal: Xu having achieved his ambition, quite indulged in extravagant luxury, with wine and women without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power, Xu gave himself over to extravagance, wine, and women without restraint.

sentences.zh: 貞元十二年四月，暴卒，時年三十三，贈司空，賻賚加等。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year of Zhenyuan he died suddenly; at the time he was thirty-three; posthumously awarded Minister of Works; funeral gifts at the enhanced grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhenyuan 12 he died suddenly at thirty-three. The court posthumously made him Minister of Works and granted enhanced funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 子三人：季和、季直、季安。

translations.literal: Three sons: Jihe, Jizhi, and Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: He left three sons: Jihe, Jizhi, and Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 季和為澶州刺史；

translations.literal: Jihe was prefect of Chanszhou;
translations.idiomatic: Jihe served as prefect of Chanszhou;

sentences.zh: 季直為衙將；

translations.literal: Jizhi was a yamen officer;
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi was a headquarters officer;

sentences.zh: 季安最幼，為嫡嗣。

translations.literal: Ji'an was the youngest and was the legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an, the youngest, was the legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 孫 季安季安字夔。

translations.literal: Grandson — Ji'an. Ji'an, style name Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an— styled Kui— was the grandson in the direct line.

sentences.zh: 母微賤，嘉誠公主蓄為己子，故寵異諸兄。

translations.literal: His mother was humble and lowly; Princess Jiacheng raised him as her own son, and for this reason he was favored above his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: His birth mother was of humble rank, but Princess Jiacheng reared him as her own, and so he was favored above his brothers.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，授左衛冑曹參軍，改著作佐郎、兼侍御史，充魏博節度副大使；

translations.literal: At several years of age he was appointed Left Guard Armory Aide; was changed to Assistant Editing Secretary and concurrent Palace Censor, serving as Weibo deputy military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: While still a small child he was made an aide in the Left Guard armory, then Assistant Editing Secretary and concurrent palace censor, and appointed deputy Weibo commissioner;

sentences.zh: 累加至試光祿少卿、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Cumulative promotions reached Acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: he rose cumulatively to acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 緒卒時，季安年纔十五，軍人推為留後，朝廷因授起復左金吾衛將軍，兼魏州大都督府長史、魏博節度營田觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: When Xu died, Ji'an was only fifteen; the soldiers installed him as acting commissioner; the court thereupon appointed him, without mourning leave, Left Gold Crow Guard general, concurrent chief administrator of the Weizhou metropolitan prefecture, and Weibo Military, Garrison-Farming, Surveillance, and Disposal Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu died Ji'an was only fifteen; the troops chose him acting commissioner, and the court appointed him Left Gold Crow Guard general without requiring him to leave mourning— along with the posts of chief administrator of Weizhou and full Weibo military and civil commissioner.

sentences.zh: 服闋，拜銀青光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射，進位檢校司空，襲封鴈門郡王。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Silver Blue-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; advanced to Acting Minister of Works; inherited the enfeoffment as Prince of Yanmen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he received Silver Blue-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Right Vice Director of State Affairs, acting Minister of Works, and inherited the title Prince of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加金紫光祿大夫，以本官同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made Golden Purple-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and, retaining his existing posts, Co-Equal to the Secretariat and Chancellery, Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was further promoted to Golden Purple-Glitter Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councilor while retaining his existing offices.

sentences.zh: 季安幼守父業，懼嘉誠之嚴，雖無他才能，亦粗修禮法；

translations.literal: Ji'an in youth guarded his father's enterprise, feared Jiacheng's strictness; though without other talent or ability, he still roughly observed ritual and law;
translations.idiomatic: While young Ji'an held to his father's legacy and, in awe of Princess Jiacheng's strictness, observed propriety as best he could despite little talent of his own;

sentences.zh: 及公主薨，遂頗自恣，擊鞠、從禽色之娛。

translations.literal: when the princess died he then quite gave rein to himself, pursuing cuju, hunting, and the pleasures of wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: but after the princess died he indulged freely in ball games, hunting, and the pleasures of wine and women.

sentences.zh: 其軍中政務，大抵任徇情意，賔僚將校，言皆不從。

translations.literal: Within the army, civil and military affairs for the most part followed whatever pleased his feelings; guests, aides, and officers—all their words he would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: Army affairs he handled entirely by whim; neither staff nor generals could sway him.

sentences.zh: 免公主喪，加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When exempted from mourning for the princess, he was promoted to Acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period for the princess ended, he was made acting Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 元和中，王承宗擅襲戎帥，憲宗命吐突承璀為招撫使，會諸軍進討。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Wang Chengzong presumptuously seized the military command; Emperor Xianzong ordered Tuzu Chenghui as pacification commissioner to assemble the various armies for advance and punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe period Wang Chengzong seized command without authorization; Emperor Xianzong appointed Tuzu Chenghui pacification commissioner and gathered allied armies to march against him.

sentences.zh: 季安亦遣大將率兵赴會，仍自供糧餉。

translations.literal: Ji'an also dispatched a great general to lead troops to the assembly, still supplying provisions from his own stores.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an sent a senior general with troops to join the campaign and supplied the rations himself.

sentences.zh: 師還，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops came home he was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 季安性忍酷，無所畏懼。

translations.literal: Ji'an's nature was cruel and harsh, without anything to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an was ruthless and feared nothing.

sentences.zh: 有進士丘絳者，嘗為田緒從事，及季安為帥，絳與同職侯臧不恊，相持爭權。

translations.literal: There was a successful candidate Qiujiang who once served as Tian Xu's staff officer; when Ji'an became commander, Qiujiang and fellow officer Hou Zang were not in accord, mutually holding out and struggling for power.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi named Qiujiang had served on Tian Xu's staff; when Ji'an took command, Qiujiang feuded with his colleague Hou Zang over power.

sentences.zh: 季安怒，斥絳為下縣尉，使人召還，先掘坎於路左，旣至坎所，活排而瘞之，其兇暴如此。

translations.literal: Ji'an was angry, demoted Qiujiang to a low county sheriff, sent men to summon him back; first dug a pit on the left of the road; when he reached the pit site, alive they pushed him in and buried him—such was his fierce brutality.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Ji'an banished Qiujiang to a lowly county post, then recalled him— only to have a pit dug beside the road. When Qiujiang arrived he was thrown in alive and buried. Such was his savagery.

sentences.zh: 元和七年卒，時年三十二，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanhe he died; at the time he was thirty-two; posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanhe 7 at the age of thirty-two; the court posthumously named him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子懷諫、懷禮、懷詢、懷讓。

translations.literal: Sons: Huaijian, Huaili, Huaixun, and Huairang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Huaijian, Huaili, Huaixun, and Huairang.

sentences.zh: 懷諫母，元誼女。

translations.literal: Huaijian's mother was the daughter of Yuan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijian's mother was a daughter of Yuan Yi.

sentences.zh: 及季安卒，元氏召諸將欲立懷諫，衆皆唯唯。

translations.literal: When Ji'an died, the Yuan clan summoned the generals intending to install Huaijian; the masses all murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji'an died, Yuan Yi summoned the generals to install Huaijian, and they murmured their assent.

sentences.zh: 懷諫幼，未能御事，軍政無巨細皆取決於私白身蔣士則，數以愛憎移易將校。

translations.literal: Huaijian was young and could not manage affairs; military and civil matters large and small all depended on the private commoner Jiang Shize, who repeatedly shifted officers according to favor and dislike.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijian was too young to rule; all military affairs, great and small, fell to a private citizen named Jiang Shize, who reshuffled commanders according to his personal likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 衙軍怒，取前臨清鎮將田興為留後，遣懷諫歸第，殺蔣士則等十餘人。

translations.literal: The yamen army was angered, selected former Linqing garrison commander Tian Xing as acting commissioner, sent Huaijian back to his residence, and killed Jiang Shize and more than ten others.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters guard rebelled, chose the former Linqing commander Tian Xing as acting commissioner, sent Huaijian home, and killed Jiang Shize and more than a dozen others.

sentences.zh: 田興葬季安畢，送懷諫於京師，乃起復授右監門衛將軍，賜第一區，芻米甚厚。

translations.literal: Tian Xing, after burying Ji'an, sent Huaijian to the capital; then without mourning appointed him Right Gate Guard general, granted one mansion, with fodder and grain very generous.
translations.idiomatic: After burying Ji'an, Tian Xing sent Huaijian to the capital, where the court restored him from mourning as Right Gate Guard general, gave him a mansion, and granted lavish provisions.

sentences.zh: 田氏自承嗣據魏州至懷諫，四世相傳襲四十九年，而田興代焉。

translations.literal: The Tian clan from Chengsi holding Weizhou to Huaijian—four generations transmitted in succession for forty-nine years—and then Tian Xing replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: From Tian Chengsi's seizure of Weizhou through Huaijian the Tian family held power for four generations and forty-nine years— until Tian Xing took their place.

sentences.zh: 田弘正，本名興。

translations.literal: Tian Hongzheng, original name Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng — whose original name was Xing.

sentences.zh: 祖延惲，魏博節度使承嗣之季父也，位終安東都護府司馬。

translations.literal: Grandfather Yanyun was Chengsi's youngest uncle, military commissioner of Weibo; he ended his post as military aide of the Andong Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tian Yanyun was the youngest uncle of military commissioner Tian Chengsi and ended his career as aide in the Andong Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 延惲生廷玠，幼敦儒雅，不樂軍職，起家為平舒丞，遷樂壽、清池、束城、河間四縣令，所至以良吏稱。

translations.literal: Yanyun begot Tingjie; in youth devoted to Confucian elegance, he did not delight in military posts; began his career as magistrate of Pingshu, transferred through four county magistracies— Leshou, Qingchi, Shucheng, and Hejian— and wherever he went was called a good official.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyun's son Tingjie was raised on the classics and shunned military life. He began as magistrate of Pingshu and served successively as magistrate of Leshou, Qingchi, Shucheng, and Hejian, winning praise as an upright administrator wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，累官至太府卿、滄州別駕，遷滄州刺史、兼御史中丞，充橫海軍使。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he cumulatively reached Grand Custodian of the Imperial Treasury and Cangzhou Vice Prefect; was transferred to Cangzhou prefect and concurrent Palace Censor and Vice Censor-in-Chief, serving as Henghai army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign he rose to Grand Custodian of the Imperial Treasury and vice prefect of Cangzhou, then became prefect of Cangzhou, vice censor-in-chief, and Henghai army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 承嗣與淄青李正己、恒州李寶臣不恊，承嗣旣令廷玠守滄州，而寶臣、朱滔聯兵攻擊，欲兼其土宇。

translations.literal: Chengsi was not in accord with Ziqing Li Zhengji and Hengzhou Li Baochen; Chengsi had already had Tingjie guard Cangzhou, and Baochen and Zhu Tao joined armies in attack, wishing to annex his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was at odds with Li Zhengji of Ziqing and Li Baochen of Hengzhou. After posting Tingjie to defend Cangzhou, Baochen and Zhu Tao joined forces to seize his territory.

sentences.zh: 廷玠嬰城固守，連年受敵，兵盡食竭，人易子而食，卒無叛者，卒能保全城守。

translations.literal: Tingjie relied on the city in firm defense, year after year under attack; troops exhausted, food depleted, men exchanging children to eat; in the end none rebelled, and in the end he was able to preserve the city and its defense.
translations.idiomatic: Tingjie held the city through years of siege until arms and grain were gone and men traded their children for food. Yet no one deserted him, and the walls stood.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，遷洺州刺史，又改相州。

translations.literal: The court praised this, transferred him to Luozhou prefect, then changed him to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended his defense and moved him to prefect of Luozhou, then of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬薛崿之亂，承嗣蠶食薛嵩所部；

translations.literal: It coincided with Xue E's rebellion; Chengsi nibbled away at the territories under Xue Song;
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil following Xue E's rebellion, Chengsi gradually swallowed the lands once held by Xue Song;

sentences.zh: 廷玠守正字民，不以宗門回避而改節。

translations.literal: Tingjie guarded rectitude and cared for the people, not because of clan ties avoiding and changing his principles.
translations.idiomatic: Tingjie governed with integrity and never softened his rule out of family loyalty.

sentences.zh: 建中初，族姪悅代承嗣領軍政，志圖兇逆，慮廷玠不從，召為節度副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, clan nephew Yue replaced Chengsi in leading military and civil affairs, scheming treacherous rebellion; fearing Tingjie would not follow, summoned him as deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong reign his kinsman Tian Yue succeeded Chengsi and plotted rebellion. Expecting Tingjie would not go along, Yue recalled him as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 悅姦謀頗露，廷玠謂悅曰：「爾藉伯父遺業，可稟守朝廷法度，坐享富貴，何苦與恒、鄆同為叛臣？

translations.literal: Yue's treacherous plot was quite exposed; Tingjie said to Yue: "You rely on your uncle's inherited enterprise—you could respect and observe court law, sit and enjoy wealth and honor—why suffer alongside Heng and Yan in becoming rebel ministers?
translations.idiomatic: When Yue's designs grew plain, Tingjie warned him: "You hold power your uncle left you. Obey the court's laws and live in honor— why join the rebels of Heng and Yan?

sentences.zh: 自兵亂已來，謀叛國家者，可以歷數，鮮有保完宗族者。

translations.literal: Since military disorder began, those who plotted rebellion against the state can be counted in succession; few have preserved and completed their clans.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, traitors have been beyond counting, and scarcely one has saved his entire house.

sentences.zh: 爾若狂志不悛，可先殺我，無令我見田氏之赤族也。」

translations.literal: If your mad ambition is not repented, you may first kill me—do not let me see the Tian clan exterminated to the last.
translations.idiomatic: If you will not abandon this mad course, kill me first— do not make me watch the Tian family wiped out.

sentences.zh: 乃謝病不出。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pleaded illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: With that he pleaded illness and refused to appear.

sentences.zh: 悅過其第而謝之，廷玠杜門不納，將吏請納。

translations.literal: Yue passed by his residence to apologize; Tingjie closed the door and did not admit him; officers and officials asked that he be admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yue came to his door to apologize, but Tingjie shut him out. His staff urged him to relent.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，鬱憤而卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong he died of pent grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 3 he died of grief and indignation.

sentences.zh: 弘正，廷玠之第二子。

translations.literal: Hongzheng was Tingjie's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng was the second son of Tian Tingjie.

sentences.zh: 少習儒書，頗通兵法，善騎射，勇而有禮，伯父承嗣愛重之。

translations.literal: In youth he studied Confucian books, was quite versed in military methods, skilled at riding and shooting, brave yet with propriety; uncle Chengsi loved and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the classics in youth, knew military arts, rode and shot well, and combined courage with courtesy; his uncle Chengsi prized him highly.

sentences.zh: 當季安之世，為衙內兵馬使。

translations.literal: During Ji'an's time he was yamen interior horse-and-arms commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ji'an he served as commander of the headquarters guard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 季安惟務侈靡，不卹軍務，屢行殺罰，弘正每從容規諷，軍中甚賴之。

translations.literal: Ji'an only pursued extravagance and indulgence, did not concern himself with military affairs, repeatedly carried out killings and punishments; Hongzheng each time with composure admonished and remonstrated by indirection, and the army greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an cared only for luxury and neglected military duties, imposing executions and punishments at will; Hongzheng gently counseled him in indirect remonstrance, and the troops came to depend on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 季安以人情歸附，乃出為臨清鎮將，欲捃摭其過害之。

translations.literal: Ji'an because popular sentiment turned toward him, thereupon posted him out as Linqing garrison commander, intending to gather his faults and harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Because the men had grown attached to Hongzheng, Ji'an transferred him to command the Linqing garrison, hoping to collect evidence of misconduct and destroy him.

sentences.zh: 弘正假以風痺請告，灸灼滿身，季安謂其無能為。

translations.literal: Hongzheng falsely cited wind paralysis to request leave, moxibustion burns covering his body, Ji'an thought he could do nothing.
