translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng feigned rheumatism to take sick leave, his body covered with moxibustion scars, and Ji'an concluded he posed no threat.

sentences.zh: 及季安病篤，其子懷諫幼騃，乃召弘正署其舊職。

translations.literal: When Ji'an's illness became grave, his son Huaijian was young and dull, thereupon summoned Hongzheng to take charge of his former post.
translations.idiomatic: As Ji'an lay dying and his son Huaijian proved young and inept, he recalled Hongzheng to his former command.

sentences.zh: 季安卒，懷諫委家僮蔣士則改易軍政，人情不悅，咸曰：「都知兵馬使田興可為吾帥也。」

translations.literal: Ji'an died; Huaijian entrusted his house slave Jiang Shize to change military administration; popular sentiment was displeased; all said: 'The army-commissioner Tian Xing can be our commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji'an's death, Huaijian put his house slave Jiang Shize in charge of reshaping military administration; the troops grew restless and declared, 'Army Commissioner Tian Xing ought to be our commander.

sentences.zh: 衙兵數千詣興私第陳請，興拒關不出，衆呼噪不已。

translations.literal: Several thousand guard soldiers went to Xing's private residence to state their petition; Xing barred the gate and would not come out; the crowd clamored without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand guard soldiers went to Xing's private residence to petition him, but he barred the gates and refused to emerge as the crowd clamored without cease.

sentences.zh: 興出，衆環而拜，請入府署。

translations.literal: Xing came out; the crowd surrounded him and bowed, requesting entry to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing finally emerged, the men surrounded him and kowtowed, begging him to enter headquarters and take command.

sentences.zh: 興頓仆於地，久之，度終不免，乃令於軍中曰：「三軍不以興不肖，令主軍務，欲與諸軍前約，當聽命否？」

translations.literal: Xing collapsed to the ground; after a long while, judging he could not escape, he ordered to the army: 'The three armies do not disdain Xing's unworthiness in putting me in charge of military affairs; I wish to make a prior agreement with you all—will you obey orders?
translations.idiomatic: Xing collapsed to the ground; after a long while, seeing no escape, he addressed the army: 'You do not disdain my unworthiness by putting me in charge. Before we go forward I want a prior agreement with you all—will you obey my orders?

sentences.zh: 咸曰：「惟命是從。」

translations.literal: All said: 'We will obey whatever is commanded.'
translations.idiomatic: They all answered, 'We will obey whatever you command.'

sentences.zh: 興曰：「吾欲守天子法，以六州版籍請吏，勿犯副大使，可乎？」

translations.literal: Xing said: 'I wish to uphold the Son of Heaven's law, offer the six prefectures' registers to civil officials, and not harm the vice commissioner—is that acceptable?'
translations.idiomatic: Xing said, 'I wish to uphold the emperor's law and offer the six prefectures' registers to the civil officials—and not harm the vice commissioner. Is that acceptable?'

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: All said: 'Agreed.'
translations.idiomatic: They all said, 'Agreed.'

sentences.zh: 是日，入府視事，殺蔣士則十數人而已。

translations.literal: That day he entered headquarters to handle affairs, killing only Jiang Shize and about ten others.
translations.idiomatic: That day he entered headquarters to take up command, executing only Jiang Shize and about ten others.

sentences.zh: 晚自府歸第，其兄融責興曰：「爾卒不能自晦，取禍之道也。」

translations.literal: In the evening, returning from headquarters to his residence, his elder brother Rong rebuked Xing: 'You ultimately cannot hide your light—this is the way to invite disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That evening, returning from headquarters to his residence, his elder brother Rong rebuked him: 'You ultimately cannot hide your light—this is the way to invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 翌日，具事上聞，憲宗嘉之，加興銀青光祿大夫、檢校工部尚書、魏州大都督府長史、兼御史大夫、上柱國、沂國公，充魏、博等州節度觀察處置支度營田等使，仍賜名弘正。

translations.literal: The next day he reported everything to the throne; Emperor Xianzong praised him, promoted Xing to Silver Blue Light Grand Master, Acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of Weizhou metropolitan prefecture, concurrent Censor-in-chief, Upper Pillar of State, Duke of Yi Kingdom, and appointed him military governor and commissioner over Wei, Bo, and other prefectures, still bestowing the name Hongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he reported everything to the throne; Emperor Xianzong praised him and promoted Xing to Silver Blue Light Grand Master, Acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of Weizhou metropolitan prefecture, concurrent Censor-in-chief, Upper Pillar of State, and Duke of Yi, appointing him military governor and commissioner over Wei, Bo, and other prefectures, and bestowing the name Hongzheng.

sentences.zh: 仍令中書舍人裴度使魏州宣慰，賜魏博三軍賞錢一百五十萬貫。

translations.literal: He still ordered Secretariat Drafting Academician Pei Du to go to Weizhou to proclaim consolation, granting the Wei-Bo three armies a reward of 1.5 million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The court also dispatched Secretariat Drafting Academician Pei Du to Weizhou to deliver imperial consolation and granted the Wei-Bo armies a reward of 1.5 million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 弘正旣受節鉞，上表曰：「臣聞君臣父子，是謂大倫，爰立紀綱，以正上下。

translations.literal: Once Hongzheng had received the seals and banners, he memorialized: 'Your subject has heard that lord and minister, father and son, are called the great bonds, establishing order to set high and low aright.
translations.idiomatic: Once invested with the commander's seals and banners, Hongzheng memorialized: 'Your subject has heard that lord and minister, father and son, are the great bonds of human society, by which order is established to set high and low aright.

sentences.zh: 其或子不為子，臣不為臣，覆載莫可得容，幽明所宜共殛。

translations.literal: If a son is not a son, a subject not a subject, heaven and earth can no longer shelter him, and spirits above and below ought jointly to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: If a son is not a son and a subject not a subject, heaven and earth can no longer shelter him, and the spirits above and below ought jointly to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 臣家本邊塞，累代唐人，從乃祖乃父以來，沐文子文孫之化。

translations.literal: Your subject's family originates on the frontier; for generations we have been men of Tang; from my grandfathers and fathers downward I have bathed in the civilizing rule of cultured generations.
translations.idiomatic: My family originates on the frontier; for generations we have been men of Tang, and from my grandfathers and fathers downward I have bathed in the civilizing rule of cultured generations.

sentences.zh: 臣幸因宗族，早列偏裨，驅馳戎馬之鄉，不睹朝廷之禮。

translations.literal: Your subject, fortunate through clan ties, early took rank among junior officers, racing through lands of warhorses without seeing the court's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate through clan ties, I early took rank among junior officers, racing through lands of warhorses without ever seeing the court's rites.

sentences.zh: 惟忠與孝，天與臣心，常思奮不顧生，以身殉國，無由上達，私自感傷。

translations.literal: Loyalty and filial piety Heaven placed in my heart; I long thought to dash forward heedless of death and give my body for the state, yet with no way to reach Your Majesty, I grieved in private.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had planted loyalty and filial piety in my heart; I often dreamed of charging forward heedless of death to give my body for the state, yet with no way to reach Your Majesty I could only grieve in private.

sentences.zh: 豈意命偶昌時，事緣難故，白刃之下，謬見推崇。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that my lot would meet a flourishing age and affairs would turn on difficult circumstances—under drawn blades I was mistakenly raised up.
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that my lot would meet a flourishing age and that affairs would turn on difficult circumstances—under drawn blades I was mistakenly raised up.

sentences.zh: 天慈遽臨，免書罪累，朝章荐及，仍委旂旄。

translations.literal: Heaven's grace suddenly descended, pardoning my accumulated faults; court honors heaped upon me, and I was entrusted with command banners.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's grace suddenly descended, pardoning my accumulated faults; court honors heaped upon me, and the command banners were placed in my hands.

sentences.zh: 錫封壤於全藩，列班榮於八座，君父之恩已極，絲毫之効未伸，但以靦冒知羞，低徊自愧。

translations.literal: Fief granted over a whole commandery, rank listed among the eight chief ministers—the grace of lord and father has reached its limit, yet not the slightest merit has been rendered; I only know shame at presumption and hang my head in self-reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Fief granted over a whole commandery, rank listed among the eight chief ministers—the grace of lord and father has reached its limit, yet I have rendered not the slightest service; I only blush at my presumption and hang my head in shame.

sentences.zh: 是知功榮所著，必俟危亂之時；

translations.literal: From this one knows that merit and glory must await times of peril and disorder;
translations.idiomatic: From this one learns that merit and glory are won only in times of peril and disorder;

sentences.zh: 徼幸之來，却在清平之日。

translations.literal: the coming of undeserved fortune, by contrast, falls in days of peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: undeserved fortune, by contrast, arrives in days of peace and order.

sentences.zh: 循涯揣分，以寵為憂。

translations.literal: Measuring myself against the shore of my worth, I take favor as cause for anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring myself against the limits of my worth, I regard favor as cause for anxiety.

sentences.zh: 伏自天寶已還，幽陵肇亂，山東奧壤，悉化戎墟。

translations.literal: Since the Tianbao era, Youling first rebelled, and the deep lands east of the mountains all turned to martial wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tianbao era, Youling first rebelled, and the rich lands east of the mountains all became martial wasteland.

sentences.zh: 外撫車馬，內懷梟獍，官封代襲，刑賞自專，國家含垢匿瑕，垂六十載。

translations.literal: Outwardly they placated chariots and horses; inwardly they harbored wolf and jackal hearts; office and fief passed by inheritance, punishments and rewards were their own—the state swallowed affronts and hid flaws for nearly sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly they placated chariots and horses; inwardly they harbored wolfish hearts; office and fief passed by inheritance, punishments and rewards were their own—the state swallowed affronts and hid flaws for nearly sixty years.

sentences.zh: 臣每思此事，當食忘餐。

translations.literal: Each time your subject reflects on this, he forgets his meal while eating.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I reflect on this, I forget my meal while eating.

sentences.zh: 若稍假天年，得奉宸算，兼弱攻昧，批亢擣虛，竭鷹犬之資，展獲禽之用，導揚和氣，洗滌偽風，然後退歸田園，以避賢路。

translations.literal: If Heaven grants me a few more years to serve Your Majesty's long design, to join the weak in attacking the blind, to strike the throat and raid the empty places, exhaust the strength of hawk and hound to display the use of captured quarry, to guide and spread harmonious qi and wash away false custom—then I would retire to field and garden and yield the path for the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven grants me a few more years to serve Your Majesty's long design—to join the weak in attacking the blind, strike the throat and raid the empty places, exhaust the strength of hawk and hound to display the use of captured quarry, guide and spread harmonious qi, and wash away false custom—then I would retire to field and garden and yield the path for the worthy.

sentences.zh: 臣懷此志，陛下察之。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds this resolve—may Your Majesty discern it.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds this resolve—may Your Majesty see it clearly.

sentences.zh: 優詔襃美。

translations.literal: An edict of commendation was issued in response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 弘正樂聞前代忠孝立功之事，於府舍起書樓，聚書萬餘卷，視事之隟，與賔佐講論古今言行可否。

translations.literal: Hongzheng took pleasure in hearing of loyalty and filial piety and achievement in earlier ages; in his headquarters he built a book tower, gathered more than ten thousand scrolls, and in intervals between handling affairs discussed with guests and aides whether ancient and modern conduct was right or wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng delighted in accounts of loyalty, filial piety, and achievement from earlier ages; in his headquarters he built a book tower, gathered more than ten thousand scrolls, and in intervals between handling affairs discussed with guests and aides whether conduct ancient and modern was right or wrong.

sentences.zh: 今河朔有沂公史例十卷，弘正客為弘正所著也。

translations.literal: Today in Hebei there is Records of Duke Yi in Ten Scrolls, written by Hongzheng's retainers for Hongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Today in Hebei there survives Records of Duke Yi in Ten Scrolls, compiled by Hongzheng's retainers on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 魏州自承嗣已來，館宇服玩有踰常制者，悉命徹毀之，以正廳大侈不居，乃視事于採訪使廳。

translations.literal: Since Chengsi's time in Weizhou, buildings, furnishings, and trappings that exceeded ordinary standards were all ordered dismantled and destroyed; because the main hall was too extravagantly large to occupy, he conducted business from the Recruitment Commissioner hall.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chengsi's time in Weizhou, buildings, furnishings, and trappings that exceeded ordinary standards were all ordered dismantled and destroyed; finding the main hall too extravagantly large to occupy, he conducted business from the Recruitment Commissioner hall.

sentences.zh: 賔僚參佐，請之於朝。

translations.literal: Guests, staff, and aides he requested from the court.
translations.idiomatic: He requested guests, staff, and aides from the court.

sentences.zh: 頗好儒書，尤通史氏，左傳、國史，知其大略。

translations.literal: He greatly favored Confucian texts and was especially versed in historical works—he knew the general outlines of the Zuo Commentary and the National Histories.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly favored Confucian texts and was especially versed in historical works, knowing the general outlines of the Zuo Commentary and the National Histories.

sentences.zh: 自弘正歸國，幽、恒、鄆、蔡有齒寒之懼，屢遣客間說，多方誘阻，而弘正終始不移其操。

translations.literal: Since Hongzheng returned to allegiance, You, Heng, Yun, and Cai felt the chill of neighboring teeth; they repeatedly sent envoys to intrigue and in many ways tried to lure and obstruct, yet Hongzheng from beginning to end did not shift his principles.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hongzheng returned to allegiance, You, Heng, Yun, and Cai felt the chill of neighboring teeth; they repeatedly sent envoys to intrigue and in many ways tried to lure and obstruct him, yet Hongzheng from beginning to end did not shift his principles.

sentences.zh: 裴度明理體，詞說雄辯，弘正聽其言，終夕不倦，遂深相結納，由是奉上之意逾謹。

translations.literal: Pei Du understood principles and governance, his words forceful and eloquent; Hongzheng listened to him without tiring all night, and they formed a deep bond—whereby his intent to serve the throne grew ever more careful.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du grasped principles and governance, his discourse forceful and eloquent; Hongzheng listened all night without tiring, and they formed a deep bond—whereupon his devotion to the throne grew ever more scrupulous.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，朝廷用兵討吳元濟，弘正遣子布率兵三千進討，屢戰有功。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe the court deployed troops against Wu Yuanji; Hongzheng sent his son Bu leading three thousand men to advance, fighting repeatedly with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanhe the court raised troops against Wu Yuanji; Hongzheng sent his son Bu at the head of three thousand men to join the campaign, winning repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 李師道以弘正効忠，又襲其後，不敢顯助元濟，故絕其掎角之援，王師得致討焉。

translations.literal: Li Shidao, because Hongzheng served loyally and also struck at his rear, dared not openly aid Yuanji, thus cutting off pincer support—the imperial armies were able to mount their campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Shidao saw Hongzheng serving loyally and striking at his rear, he dared not openly aid Yuanji, thus cutting off pincer support and allowing the imperial armies to mount their campaign.

sentences.zh: 俄而王承宗叛，詔弘正以全師壓境，承宗懼，遣使求救於弘正，遂表其事，承宗遂納二子，獻德、棣二州以自解。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Chengzong rebelled; the edict ordered Hongzheng to press the border with his full army; Chengzong feared this and sent envoys begging Hongzheng for rescue; Hongzheng reported the matter, and Chengzong thereupon surrendered two sons and offered De and Di prefectures to extricate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Chengzong rebelled; the edict ordered Hongzheng to press the border with his full army. Chengzong feared this and sent envoys begging Hongzheng for rescue; Hongzheng reported the matter, and Chengzong thereupon surrendered two sons and offered De and Di prefectures to extricate himself.

sentences.zh: 十三年，王師加兵於鄆，詔弘正與宣武、義成、武寧、橫海等五鎮之師會軍齊進。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year imperial troops added forces at Yun; Hongzheng was ordered to join the armies of five commands—Xuanwu, Yicheng, Wuning, and Henghai—in a united advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the imperial armies reinforced at Yun; Hongzheng was ordered to unite with the forces of five commands—Xuanwu, Yicheng, Wuning, and Henghai—and advance together.

sentences.zh: 十一月，弘正自帥全師自楊劉渡河築壘，距鄆四十里。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Hongzheng personally led his full force across the Yellow River at Yangliu and built fortifications forty li from Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Hongzheng personally led his full army across the Yellow River at Yangliu and built fortifications forty li from Yun.

sentences.zh: 師道遣大將劉悟率重兵以抗弘正，結壘相望。

translations.literal: Shidao sent his great general Liu Wu with heavy troops to resist Hongzheng; they built opposing camps facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao dispatched his great general Liu Wu with a heavy force to oppose Hongzheng; the two sides built opposing camps facing each other.

sentences.zh: 前後合戰，魏軍大捷，而李愬、李光顏三面進攻，賊皆挫敗，其勢將危。

translations.literal: In repeated battles the Wei army won great victories, while Li Su and Li Guangyan attacked on three sides; the rebels were all broken, and their situation grew perilous.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated engagements the Wei army won great victories, while Li Su and Li Guangyan pressed in from three sides; the rebels were everywhere broken, and their position grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月，劉悟以河上之衆倒戈入鄆，斬師道首，詣弘正請降。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year Liu Wu turned his troops on the river in mutiny, entered Yun, beheaded Shidao, and came to Hongzheng to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourteenth year Liu Wu turned the troops on the river in mutiny, entered Yun, beheaded Shidao, and came to Hongzheng to surrender.

sentences.zh: 淄青十二州平，論功加檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The twelve prefectures of Ziqing were pacified; for merit he was promoted to Acting Grand Mentor, Co-Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve prefectures of Ziqing were pacified; for his merit he was promoted to Acting Grand Mentor and Co-Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，弘正入覲，憲宗待之隆異，對於麟德殿，參佐將校二百餘人皆有頒錫，進加檢校司徒、兼侍中，實封三百戶。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month Hongzheng entered court audience; Emperor Xianzong received him with extraordinary honor, holding audience at Linde Hall; over two hundred aides and generals all received bestowments; he was further promoted Acting Grand Mentor, Concurrent Palace Secretary, with three hundred taxable households as permanent fief.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the eighth month Hongzheng entered court audience; Emperor Xianzong received him with extraordinary honor, holding audience at Linde Hall; over two hundred aides and generals all received bestowments; he was further promoted Acting Grand Mentor and Concurrent Palace Secretary, with three hundred taxable households as permanent fief.

sentences.zh: 仍以其兄檢校刑部尚書、相州刺史融為太子賔客，東都留司。

translations.literal: His elder brother Rong, Acting Minister of Punishments and prefect of Xiangzhou, was made Crown Prince's Guest and Eastern Capital Remission Officer.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Rong, Acting Minister of Punishments and prefect of Xiangzhou, was appointed Crown Prince's Guest and Eastern Capital Remission Officer.

sentences.zh: 弘正三上章，願留闕下，憲宗勞之曰：「昨韓弘至朝，稱疾懇辭戎務，朕不得不從。

translations.literal: Hongzheng thrice submitted memorials begging to remain at court; Emperor Xianzong comforted him: 'Yesterday Han Hong came to court and earnestly pleaded illness to decline military affairs—I had no choice but to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng thrice submitted memorials begging to remain at court; Emperor Xianzong comforted him, saying, 'Yesterday Han Hong came to court and earnestly pleaded illness to decline military affairs—I had no choice but to grant it.

sentences.zh: 今卿復請留，意誠可尚，然魏土樂卿之政，隣境服卿之威，為我長城，不可辭也。

translations.literal: Now you again ask to remain; your intention is truly admirable. Yet the people of Wei are pleased with your governance, neighboring borders respect your authority—you are my long wall; you cannot decline.
translations.idiomatic: Now you again ask to remain; your intention is truly admirable. Yet the people of Wei delight in your governance, neighboring borders respect your authority—you are my long wall; you cannot decline.

sentences.zh: 可亟歸藩。」

translations.literal: You may swiftly return to the command.
translations.idiomatic: Return at once to your post.

sentences.zh: 弘正每懼有一旦之憂，嗣襲之風不革，兄弟子姪，悉仕於朝，憲宗皆擢居班列，朱紫盈庭，當時榮之。

translations.literal: Hongzheng always feared sudden calamity and that the custom of hereditary succession would not change; brothers, sons, and nephews all took office at court, and Xianzong raised them all to court ranks—purple and vermilion filled the hall; men of the time honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng always feared sudden calamity and that the custom of hereditary succession would not change; brothers, sons, and nephews all took office at court, and Xianzong raised them all to court ranks—purple and vermilion filled the hall, and men of the time honored this.

sentences.zh: 十五年十月，鎮州王承宗卒，穆宗以弘正檢校司徒、兼中書令、鎮州大都督府長史，充成德軍節度、鎮冀深趙觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifteenth year Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died; Emperor Muzong made Hongzheng Acting Grand Mentor, Concurrent Chancellery Director, chief administrator of Zhenzhou metropolitan prefecture, and military governor of Chengde with oversight of Zhen, Ji, Shen, and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifteenth year Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died; Emperor Muzong appointed Hongzheng Acting Grand Mentor, Concurrent Chancellery Director, chief administrator of Zhenzhou metropolitan prefecture, and military governor of Chengde with oversight of Zhen, Ji, Shen, and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 弘正以新與鎮人戰伐，有父兄之怨，乃以魏兵二千為衛從。

translations.literal: Hongzheng, having recently fought the men of Zhen, knew they bore grudges like those of fathers and elder brothers killed; he therefore took two thousand Wei troops as personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng, having recently fought the men of Zhen, knew they nursed grudges like those who had lost fathers and elder brothers; he therefore took two thousand Wei troops as personal guard.

sentences.zh: 十一月二十六日，至鎮州，時賜鎮州三軍賞錢一百萬貫，不時至，軍衆諠騰以為言。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month he arrived at Zhenzhou; at that time the bestowed reward of one million strings for the Zhenzhou three armies had not arrived in time, and the army masses clamored about it.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month he reached Zhenzhou; the promised reward of one million strings for the Zhenzhou armies had not yet arrived, and the troops raised an uproar.

sentences.zh: 弘正親自撫喻，人情稍安，仍表請留魏兵為紀綱之僕，以持衆心，其糧賜請給於有司。

translations.literal: Hongzheng personally comforted and addressed them; sentiment gradually settled; he still memorialized asking to retain Wei troops as disciplined retainers to hold the hearts of the masses, with their grain and rewards supplied by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng personally comforted and addressed them until sentiment gradually settled; he still memorialized asking to retain Wei troops as disciplined retainers to hold the hearts of the masses, with their grain and rewards supplied by the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 時度支使崔倰不知大體，固阻其請，凡四上表不報。

translations.literal: At the time Finance Commissioner Cui Jun did not grasp the larger picture and stubbornly blocked his request; four memorials were sent without reply.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Finance Commissioner Cui Jun did not grasp the larger picture and stubbornly blocked his request; four memorials went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 明年七月，歸卒於魏州，是月二十八日夜軍亂，弘正并家屬、參佐、將吏等三百餘口並遇害，穆宗聞之震悼，冊贈太尉，賵賻加等。

translations.literal: The next seventh month the Wei troops returned to Weizhou; on the twenty-eighth night of that month the army mutinied, and Hongzheng together with family, aides, and officers—more than three hundred souls—were all killed; Muzong was shaken and grieved; he posthumously enfeoffed him Grand Marshal and augmented the funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The next seventh month the Wei troops returned to Weizhou; on the twenty-eighth night of that month the army mutinied, and Hongzheng together with family, aides, and officers—more than three hundred souls—were all killed. Muzong was shaken and grieved; he posthumously enfeoffed him Grand Marshal and augmented the funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 弘正孝友慈惠，骨肉之恩甚厚。

translations.literal: Hongzheng was filial, fraternal, benevolent, and kind; affection among kin was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng was filial, fraternal, benevolent, and kind; affection among kin ran very deep.

sentences.zh: 兄弟子姪在兩都者數十人，競為崇飾，日費約二十萬，魏、鎮州之財，皆輦屬於道。

translations.literal: Brothers, sons, and nephews in the two capitals numbered several tens, competing in extravagance, daily expenses roughly two hundred thousand; wealth of Wei and Zhenzhou was all carted along the roads to them.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers, sons, and nephews in the two capitals numbered several tens, competing in extravagance, with daily expenses of roughly two hundred thousand; wealth from Wei and Zhenzhou was all carted along the roads to them.

sentences.zh: 河北將卒心不平之，故不能盡變其俗，竟以此致亂。

translations.literal: Hebei generals and soldiers in their hearts were not level about this; therefore he could not fully change their customs, and in the end by this he brought on disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei generals and soldiers resented this in their hearts; therefore he could not fully change their customs, and ultimately disorder came from this.

sentences.zh: 弘正子布、群、牟。

translations.literal: Hongzheng's sons: Bu, Qun, and Mou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng's sons were Bu, Qun, and Mou.

sentences.zh: 子 布布，弘正第三子。

translations.literal: Son: Bu. Bu was Hongzheng's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Son Bu—Bu was Hongzheng's third son.

sentences.zh: 始，弘正為田季安裨將，鎮臨清，布年尚幼，知季安身世必危，密白其父帥其所鎮之衆歸朝，弘正甚奇之。

translations.literal: At first, when Hongzheng was Tian Ji'an's deputy general garrisoning Linqing, Bu was still young; knowing Ji'an's line was doomed, he secretly told his father to lead the troops he commanded back to the court—Hongzheng marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Hongzheng was Tian Ji'an's deputy general garrisoning Linqing, Bu was still young; foreseeing that Ji'an's line was doomed, he secretly urged his father to lead the troops under his command back to the court—Hongzheng marveled at this.

sentences.zh: 及弘正節制魏博，布掌親兵，國家討淮、蔡，布率偏師隷嚴綬，軍於唐州，授檢校秘書監、兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: When Hongzheng took command of Wei-Bo, Bu commanded the personal guard; the state campaigned against Huai and Cai; Bu led a detached division under Yan Shou, encamped at Tangzhou, and was appointed Acting Secretariat Director and Concurrent Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng took command of Wei-Bo, Bu commanded the personal guard; when the state campaigned against Huai and Cai, Bu led a detached division under Yan Shou, encamped at Tangzhou, and was appointed Acting Secretariat Director and Concurrent Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 前後十八戰，破凌雲柵，下郾城，布皆有功，擢授御史中丞。

translations.literal: In eighteen battles he broke Lingyun stockade and took Yancheng—Bu had merit in all; he was promoted Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In eighteen engagements he broke Lingyun stockade and took Yancheng—Bu distinguished himself in all; he was promoted Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 時裴度為宣撫使，嘗觀兵於沱口，賊將董重質領驍騎遽至，布以二百騎突出溝中擊之，俄而諸軍大集，賊乃退去。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Du was pacification commissioner; he once reviewed troops at Tuokou when the rebel general Dong Chongzhi led elite cavalry suddenly arrived; Bu with two hundred riders burst from the ditch to strike them; soon the various armies massed and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Du was pacification commissioner; he once reviewed troops at Tuokou when the rebel general Dong Chongzhi led elite cavalry suddenly upon them; Bu with two hundred riders burst from the ditch to strike them; soon the various armies massed and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 淮西平，拜左金吾衛將軍、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Huai West was pacified, he was appointed Left Golden Guard general and concurrent Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Huai West he was appointed Left Golden Guard general and Concurrent Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，丁母憂，起復舊官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he entered mourning for his mother; he was raised from mourning and restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he entered mourning for his mother; he was recalled from mourning to his former post.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，弘正移鎮成德軍，仍以布為河陽三城懷節度使，父子俱擁節旄，同日拜命。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year Hongzheng transferred to Chengde command and Bu was made military governor of Heyang Three Cities Huaijie; father and son both held command banners, invested the same day.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year Hongzheng transferred to Chengde command and Bu was made military governor of Heyang Three Cities Huaijie; father and son both held command banners and received their commissions the same day.

sentences.zh: 時韓弘亦與子公武俱為節度使，然人以忠勤多田氏。

translations.literal: At the time Han Hong and his son Gongwu were both military governors, yet people thought the Tian clan more devoted and diligent.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Han Hong and his son Gongwu were both military governors, yet people judged the Tian clan the more devoted and diligent.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年春，移鎮涇原。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Changqing he moved his command to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Changqing he transferred to Jingyuan command.

sentences.zh: 其秋，鎮州軍亂，害弘正，都知兵馬使王廷湊為留後。

translations.literal: That autumn the Zhenzhou army mutinied and killed Hongzheng; the army-commissioner Wang Tingcou became acting commander.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Zhenzhou army mutinied, killed Hongzheng, and the army-commissioner Wang Tingcou became acting commander.

sentences.zh: 時魏博節度使李愬病不能軍，無以捍廷湊之亂，且以魏軍田氏舊旅，乃急詔布至，起復為魏博節度使，仍遷檢校工部尚書，令布乗傳之鎮。

translations.literal: At the time Wei-Bo military governor Li Su was too ill to take the field and could not resist Tingcou's rebellion; moreover because the Wei army was Tian's old troops, an urgent edict summoned Bu, recalled from mourning as Wei-Bo military governor, further promoted Acting Minister of Works, and ordered Bu to travel post-haste to command.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei-Bo military governor Li Su was too ill to take the field and could not resist Tingcou's rebellion; moreover, because the Wei army was Tian's old troops, an urgent edict summoned Bu, recalled from mourning as Wei-Bo military governor, further promoted Acting Minister of Works, and ordered Bu to travel post-haste to command.

sentences.zh: 布喪服居堊室，去旌節導從之飾；

translations.literal: Bu wore mourning in a thatched hut, removing banners, seals, and escort finery;
translations.idiomatic: Bu wore mourning in a thatched hut, stripping away banners, seals, and escort finery;

sentences.zh: 及入魏州，居喪御事，動皆得禮。

translations.literal: When he entered Weizhou he dwelt in mourning while handling affairs; every movement accorded with rites.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering Weizhou he handled affairs while in mourning, every act conforming to rites.

sentences.zh: 其祿俸月入百萬，一無所取，又籍魏中舊產，無巨細計錢十餘萬貫，皆出之以頒軍士。

translations.literal: His salary income of one million per month he took not one part; he also registered old property in Wei, counting great and small more than one hundred thousand strings, and all was taken out and distributed to the army soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: His monthly salary of one million he took none of; he also inventoried old family property in Wei—more than one hundred thousand strings in all—and distributed it entirely to the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 牙將史憲誠出己麾下，謂必能輸誠報効，用為先鋒兵馬使，精銳悉委之。

translations.literal: The staff commander Shi Xiancheng from his own subordinates—thinking he would surely render sincere service—was made vanguard army commissioner, and all elite troops were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Staff commander Shi Xiancheng, drawn from his own subordinates and judged sure to render sincere service, was made vanguard army commissioner, and all elite troops were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 時屢有急詔促令進軍。

translations.literal: At the time there were repeatedly urgent edicts pressing orders to advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated urgent edicts pressed him to advance.

sentences.zh: 十月，布以魏軍三萬七千討之，結壘於南宮縣之南。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Bu with thirty-seven thousand Wei troops went to punish them, building fortifications south of Nangong county.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Bu marched thirty-seven thousand Wei troops against them and built fortifications south of Nangong county.

sentences.zh: 十二月，進軍，下賊二柵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he advanced the army and took two rebel stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he advanced, capturing two rebel stockades.

sentences.zh: 時朱克融囚張弘靖，據幽州，與廷湊掎角拒命。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Kerong imprisoned Zhang Hongjing and held Youzhou, joining with Tingcou in pincer resistance to orders.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Kerong held Zhang Hongjing prisoner and occupied Youzhou, coordinating with Tingcou in pincer defiance.

sentences.zh: 河朔三鎮，素相連衡，憲誠陰有異志。

translations.literal: The three Hebei commands had always been linked in alliance; Xiancheng secretly had a different intent.
translations.idiomatic: The three Hebei commands had always been allied; Xiancheng secretly harbored different intentions.

sentences.zh: 而魏軍驕侈，怯於格戰，又屬雪寒，糧餉不給，以此愈無鬬志，憲誠從而間之。

translations.literal: Moreover the Wei army was proud and extravagant, timid in close combat; moreover it was snow and cold and provisions were not supplied—by this their fighting will grew even less, and Xiancheng followed and sowed division among them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Wei army was proud and extravagant, cowardly in close combat; with snow and cold their provisions failed—thus they lost fighting will all the more, and Xiancheng took advantage to sow discord.

sentences.zh: 俄有詔分布軍與李光顏合勢，東救深州，其衆自潰，多為憲誠所有，布得其衆八千。

translations.literal: Before long there was an edict distributing Bu's army to join forces with Li Guangyan and eastward rescue Shenzhou; the masses on their own dissolved, many coming into Xiancheng's possession; Bu obtained only eight thousand of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered Bu to divide his army and join forces with Li Guangyan to rescue Shenzhou in the east; the troops dissolved on their own, most falling to Xiancheng's control; Bu retained only eight thousand men.

sentences.zh: 是月十日，還魏州。

translations.literal: On the tenth day of that month he returned to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth of that month he returned to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 十一日，會諸將復議興師，而將卒益倨，咸曰：「尚書能行河朔舊事，則死生以之；

translations.literal: On the eleventh he convened the generals to discuss again raising the army, but officers and soldiers grew ever more arrogant, all saying: 'If the Minister can act in the old Hebei ways, we will follow him to life or death;
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh he convened the generals to discuss again raising the army, but officers and soldiers grew ever more arrogant, all saying, 'If the Minister can act in the old Hebei ways, we will follow him to life or death;

sentences.zh: 若使復戰，皆不能也。」

translations.literal: If you make us again go to battle, none can do it.
translations.idiomatic: If you make us fight again, none of us can.

sentences.zh: 布以憲誠離間，度衆終不為用，嘆曰：「功無成矣！」

translations.literal: Bu, seeing Xiancheng's sowing of discord and judging the men would never serve, sighed: 'Merit will not be achieved!'
translations.idiomatic: Bu, seeing Xiancheng's sowing of discord and judging the men would never serve, sighed, 'Merit will not be achieved!'

sentences.zh: 即日，密表陳軍情，且稱遺表，略曰：「臣觀衆意，終負國恩，臣旣無功，不敢忘死。

translations.literal: That same day he secretly memorialized reporting army conditions and also submitted what he called a final testament, stating in brief: 'Your subject observes the men's intent—they will ultimately betray the state's grace; having achieved no merit, I dare not forget death.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he secretly memorialized reporting army conditions and also submitted what he called a final testament, stating in brief, 'Your subject observes the men's intent—they will ultimately betray the state's grace; having achieved no merit, I dare not forget death.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下速救光顏、元翼，不然，則義士忠臣，皆為河朔屠害。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty quickly to rescue Guangyan and Yuanyi; if not, then righteous men and loyal subjects will all be slaughtered by Hebei.'
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray Your Majesty swiftly rescue Guangyan and Yuanyi; otherwise loyal men and true subjects will all be slaughtered by Hebei.'

sentences.zh: 奉表號哭，拜授其從事李石，乃入啟父靈，抽刀自刺，曰：「上以謝君父，下以示三軍。」

translations.literal: Weeping he presented the memorial and entrusted it to his aide Li Shi; then he entered before his father's spirit tablet, drew a knife and stabbed himself, saying: 'Above, to repay lord and father; below, to show the three armies.'
translations.idiomatic: Weeping he presented the memorial and entrusted it to his aide Li Shi; then he entered before his father's spirit tablet, drew a knife and stabbed himself, saying, 'Above, to repay lord and father; below, to show the three armies.'

sentences.zh: 言訖而絕。

translations.literal: When the words were finished he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the words ended he expired.

sentences.zh: 時議以布才雖不足，能以死謝家國，心志決烈，得燕、趙之古風焉。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time held that although Bu's talent was insufficient, he was able to use death to repay family and state—his heart and will decisive and fierce, obtaining the ancient wind of Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held that though Bu's talent was insufficient, he could give his death to repay family and state—his resolve fierce, capturing the ancient spirit of Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 穆宗聞之駭嘆，廢朝三日，詔曰：

translations.literal: Muzong on hearing it was startled and sighed; he suspended court three days and issued an edict, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Muzong on hearing this was appalled and sighed; he suspended court for three days and issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 故魏博節度使、起復寧遠將軍、檢校工部尚書、兼魏州大都督府長史、御史大夫、賜紫金魚袋田布，朕以寡昧，臨御萬邦，威刑不能禁干紀之徒，道化不能馴多僻之俗，致使上公罹禍，田氏銜冤。

translations.literal: The deceased Wei-Bo military governor, recalled-from-mourning Ningyuan general, Acting Minister of Works, concurrent chief administrator of Weizhou metropolitan prefecture, Censor-in-chief, granted purple robe and gold fish tally Tian Bu: We, few and dim, face and rule the myriad states; awe and punishment cannot restrain those who transgress the statutes, the Way's transformation cannot tame the many perverse customs—thereby causing the upper duke to meet calamity and the Tian clan to hold grievance.
translations.idiomatic: The late Wei-Bo military governor, recalled-from-mourning general of Ningyuan, Acting Minister of Works, concurrent chief administrator of Weizhou metropolitan prefecture, Censor-in-chief, granted purple robe and gold fish tally—Tian Bu: We, weak and unenlightened, preside over the myriad realms; might and punishment cannot restrain those who violate discipline, and moral transformation cannot tame a people grown wayward—thereby causing the high duke to suffer calamity and the Tian clan to bear grievance.

sentences.zh: 爰整旅以徂征，每終食而浩嘆，自茲弔伐，驟歷寒暄。

translations.literal: Thereupon I array troops and go on campaign; at every meal not finished I sigh greatly; from this condolence-and-punishment onward, suddenly seasons of cold and warmth have passed.
translations.idiomatic: I have mustered armies to march forth; at every unfinished meal I sigh deeply; since this punitive campaign began, seasons have swiftly turned.

sentences.zh: 雖良將銳師，率皆恊力；

translations.literal: Although good generals and sharp armies, for the most part all together exert strength;
translations.idiomatic: Though good generals and sharp armies for the most part all exert themselves together;

sentences.zh: 而俟時觀釁，未即齊驅。

translations.literal: Yet they wait for the opportune moment and watch for openings, not immediately advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they waited for the right moment and watched for openings, without advancing in unison at once.

sentences.zh: 嗟我誠臣，結其哀憤，引遷延之咎以自刻責，奮決烈之志以謝君親。

translations.literal: Alas, my loyal minister—gathering his grief and indignation, taking upon himself the blame for delay, rousing a resolute and fierce will to repay sovereign and parents.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, my loyal minister gathered grief and righteous anger, shouldered the fault for delay, and summoned a resolute spirit to repay sovereign and kin.

sentences.zh: 白刃置於肝心，鴻毛論其生死，忠臣孝子，一舉兩全。

translations.literal: White blade set upon liver and heart; life and death weighed as a swan's down; loyal minister and filial son—both fulfilled in a single act.
translations.idiomatic: He set the naked blade to his heart, treating life and death as lightly as a feather, fulfilling loyalty and filial piety in a single deed.

sentences.zh: 晉稱卞氏之門，漢表尸鄉之節，比方於布，今古為隣。

translations.literal: The Jin praised the house of Bian; the Han recorded the martyrdom at Shixiang; compared with Bu, ancient and modern stand as neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin exalted the house of Bian; the Han enshrined the martyrdom at Shixiang—in both ages Bu stands their equal, ancient and present side by side.

sentences.zh: 況其臨命須臾，處之不撓，載形章表，益深衷悃。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the fleeting moment before death, he bore it unflinchingly; recorded in memorials, his sincere devotion grows ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: All the more so in that final fleeting moment he met death unflinching; set down in memorials, his heartfelt devotion shines the more deeply.

sentences.zh: 問使發緘，悼心疾首。

translations.literal: When the envoy opened the sealed letter, grief pierced the heart and head.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy broke the seal, grief pierced my heart and wracked my brow.

sentences.zh: 從先臣於厚載，爾則無愧；

translations.literal: To follow former ministers in the deep earth—you have nothing to be ashamed of;
translations.idiomatic: To join the former ministers beneath the earth—you have nothing to be ashamed of;

sentences.zh: 睹遺像於麟閣，予何所堪。

translations.literal: To behold your portrait in the Qilin Pavilion—how can I bear it?
translations.idiomatic: To gaze upon your portrait in the Qilin Pavilion—how can I endure it?

sentences.zh: 端拱崇名，職垂彝典，據斯以報，聊攄永懷。

translations.literal: Upright in dignity with an honored posthumous name, his office perpetuated in eternal statute; relying on this to repay him, I briefly express my lasting grief.
translations.idiomatic: With dignified honor and a lofty posthumous name, his office enshrined in enduring statute—by this I repay him and give brief voice to my lasting grief.

sentences.zh: 可贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Vice Director of the Right of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He is to be posthumously granted the post of Vice Director of the Right of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 布子在宥，大中年為安南都護，頗立邊功。

translations.literal: Bu's son Zaiyou, in the Dazhong era served as Protector-General of Annan and achieved considerable frontier merit.
translations.idiomatic: Bu's son Zaiyou served as Protector-General of Annan in the Dazhong era and won considerable merit on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 子 群群，大和八年為少府少監，充入吐蕃使，歷棣州刺史、安南都護。

translations.literal: His son Qun, in the eighth year of Dahe served as Vice Director of the Palace Storehouses, was sent as envoy to Tibet, and later served as prefect of Di Prefecture and Protector-General of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qun, in the eighth year of the Dahe reign served as Vice Director of the Palace Storehouses, went as envoy to Tibet, and later served as prefect of Di and Protector-General of Annan.

sentences.zh: 子 牟牟，會昌初為豐州刺史、天德軍使，歷武寧軍節度使，大中朝為兗海節度使，移鎮天平軍。

translations.literal: His son Mou, at the beginning of Huichang was prefect of Feng and commissioner of the Tiande Army; he later served as military commissioner of Wuning; in the Dazhong reign he became military commissioner of Yanhai and was transferred to command the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mou, at the opening of Huichang, was prefect of Feng and commissioner of the Tiande Army; he later served as military commissioner of Wuning; in the Dazhong reign he became military commissioner of Yanhai and was transferred to Tianping.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆以邊上立功，累更藩鎮，以忠義為談者所稱。

translations.literal: All his sons earned merit on the frontier, served in succession at various military prefectures, and were praised by commentators for their loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: All his sons won merit on the frontier, served in turn at one military prefecture after another, and were praised by contemporaries for their loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 張孝忠，本奚之種類。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaozhong was originally of Xi tribal stock.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaozhong belonged to the Xi people by origin.

sentences.zh: 曾祖靖、祖遜，代乙失活部落酋帥。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jing and grandfather Xun were chieftains of the Yishihuo tribe for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jing and grandfather Xun had been chieftains of the Yishihuo tribe for generations.

sentences.zh: 父謐，開元中以衆歸國，授鴻臚卿同正，以孝忠貴，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Mi, in the Kaiyuan era brought his people to submit to the state and was appointed Acting Director of the Court of Banquets; when Xiaozhong rose to prominence, Mi was posthumously granted Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mi, in the Kaiyuan era led his people to submit to the dynasty and was appointed Acting Director of the Court of Banquets; when Xiaozhong rose to prominence, Mi was posthumously granted Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 孝忠以勇聞於燕、趙。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong was known throughout Yan and Zhao for his valor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong was famed throughout Yan and Zhao for his courage.

sentences.zh: 時號張阿勞、王沒諾干，二人齊名。

translations.literal: At the time he was called Zhang Alao and Wang Meinuogan—the two were equally renowned.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was known as Zhang Alao and Wang Wujun as Meinuogan—the two were equally famed.

sentences.zh: 阿勞，孝忠本字；

translations.literal: Alao was Xiaozhong's original courtesy name;
translations.idiomatic: 'Alao' was the courtesy name Zhang Xiaozhong bore from birth;

sentences.zh: 沒諾干，王武俊本字。

translations.literal: Meinuogan was Wang Wujun's original courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: 'Meinuogan' was Wang Wujun's original courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 孝忠形體魁偉，長六尺餘，性寬裕，事親恭孝。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong was imposing in stature, over six feet tall, generous in nature, and reverently filial toward his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong was imposing in build, more than six feet tall, open-handed by nature, and reverently filial toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，以善射授內供奉。

translations.literal: Late in the Tianbao era, for skill in archery he was appointed an inner palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianbao era he was appointed an inner palace attendant for his skill in archery.

sentences.zh: 安祿山奏為偏將，破九姓突厥，先登陷陣，以功授果毅折衝。

translations.literal: An Lushan recommended him as a subordinate general; in breaking the Nine Surname Turks he was first to charge and breach the lines; for merit he was granted the post of guoyi zhechong.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan recommended him as a subordinate general; in defeating the Nine Surname Turks he was first to scale the walls and break the enemy lines, and for this merit was granted the post of guoyi zhechong.

sentences.zh: 祿山、史思明繼陷河洛，孝忠皆為其前鋒。

translations.literal: When Lushan and Shi Siming successively overran the He and Luo regions, Xiaozhong served as their vanguard each time.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan and Shi Siming in turn overran the He and Luo heartland, Xiaozhong served each time as their vanguard.

sentences.zh: 史朝義敗，入李寶臣帳下。

translations.literal: When Shi Chaoyi was defeated, he entered the service of Li Baochen.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Chaoyi was defeated, he entered Li Baochen's service.

sentences.zh: 上元中，奏授左領軍郎將，累加左金吾衛將軍同正、試殿中監，仍賜名孝忠，歷飛狐、高陽二軍使。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he was memorialized and appointed Left Lingjun Captain; he was successively promoted to Acting Left Jinwu Guard General and Acting Director of the Palace Administration, and was granted the name Xiaozhong; he served as commissioner of the Feihu and Gaoyang garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shangyuan era he was memorialized and appointed Left Lingjun Captain; he rose in turn to Acting Left Jinwu Guard General and Acting Director of the Palace Administration, was granted the name Xiaozhong, and served as commissioner of the Feihu and Gaoyang garrisons.

sentences.zh: 李寶臣以孝忠謹重驍勇，甚委信之，以妻妹昧谷氏妻焉，仍悉以易州諸鎮兵馬令其統制。

translations.literal: Li Baochen, finding Xiaozhong prudent, steadfast, and fiercely brave, trusted him greatly; he gave Xiaozhong his wife's sister of the Megu clan in marriage and entrusted him with command over all the garrison troops of Yizhou's various posts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baochen, finding Xiaozhong prudent, steadfast, and fiercely brave, trusted him deeply; he gave Xiaozhong his wife's sister of the Megu clan in marriage and put all the garrison troops of Yizhou's border posts under his command.

sentences.zh: 前後居城鎮十餘年，甚著威惠。

translations.literal: For more than ten years he held these border posts, winning great renown for both authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he held these border posts and won great renown for both stern authority and generous kindness.

sentences.zh: 田承嗣之寇冀州也，寶臣俾孝忠以精騎數千禦之。

translations.literal: When Tian Chengsi raided Jizhou, Baochen had Xiaozhong meet him with several thousand crack horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Chengsi raided Jizhou, Baochen sent Xiaozhong against him with several thousand elite horsemen.

sentences.zh: 承嗣見其整肅，歎曰：「張阿勞在焉，冀州未易圖也。」

translations.literal: Chengsi saw how orderly his forces were and sighed: "With Zhang Alao here, Jizhou will not be easy to take.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi saw how disciplined his forces were and sighed, "With Zhang Alao here, Jizhou will not be easy to take.

sentences.zh: 乃焚營宵遁。

translations.literal: He thereupon burned his camp and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon burned his camp and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 及寶臣與朱滔戰於瓦橋，常慮滔來攻，故以孝忠為易州刺史，選精騎七千配焉，使扞幽州。

translations.literal: When Baochen fought Zhu Tao at Waqiao, he constantly feared Tao would attack, and so appointed Xiaozhong prefect of Yi, assigned him seven thousand elite horsemen, and had him defend against Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Baochen fought Zhu Tao at Waqiao, he constantly feared Tao would strike at him, and so made Xiaozhong prefect of Yi, assigned him seven thousand elite horsemen, and had him hold the line against Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 奏授太子賔客、兼御史中丞，封范陽郡王。

translations.literal: He memorialized and had Xiaozhong appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, with enfeoffment as Prince of Fanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court, and Xiaozhong was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Prince of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 旣而寶臣疑忌大將，殺李獻誠等四五人，使召孝忠，孝忠懼不往。

translations.literal: Before long Baochen grew suspicious and jealous of his major generals, killed Li Xiancheng and four or five others, and sent to summon Xiaozhong; Xiaozhong was afraid and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Baochen grew suspicious of his senior generals, killed Li Xiancheng and four or five others, and sent for Xiaozhong; Xiaozhong was afraid and did not go.

sentences.zh: 寶臣使孝忠弟孝節召焉，孝忠命孝節復命曰：「諸將無狀，連頸受戮，孝忠懼死不敢往，亦不敢叛，猶公之不覲於朝，慮禍而已，無他志也。」

translations.literal: Baochen sent Xiaozhong's younger brother Xiaojie to summon him; Xiaozhong ordered Xiaojie to report back: "The generals behaved badly and were beheaded one after another; Xiaozhong fears death and dares not come, yet dares not rebel either—it is like your lord not attending court, merely dreading calamity, with no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen sent Xiaozhong's younger brother Xiaojie to summon him; Xiaozhong told Xiaojie to report back, "The generals have misbehaved and been beheaded in succession; Xiaozhong fears death and dares not come, yet he dares not rebel either—it is like your lord not appearing at court, dreading disaster and nothing more, with no other design.

sentences.zh: 孝節泣曰：「兄不行，吾歸死矣。」

translations.literal: Xiaojie wept and said: "If you, elder brother, will not go, I return to my death."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie wept and said, "If you will not go, brother, I return to my death."

sentences.zh: 孝忠曰：「偕往則并命，吾留無患也。」

translations.literal: Xiaozhong said: "If we go together we perish together; if I stay there is no harm."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong said, "If we go together we die together; if I stay, there will be no trouble."

sentences.zh: 乃歸，果無患。

translations.literal: So he returned, and indeed there was no harm.
translations.idiomatic: So he returned, and indeed there was no trouble.

sentences.zh: 無幾，寶臣死，其子惟岳阻兵不受命，朝廷詔幽州節度使討之。

translations.literal: Before long Baochen died; his son Weiyue raised troops and defied orders; the court ordered the Youzhou military commissioner to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Baochen died; his son Weiyue raised troops and refused to obey orders; the court ordered the Youzhou military commissioner to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 滔以孝忠宿將善戰，有精兵八千在易州，慮軍興則撓其後，乃使判官蔡雄說孝忠曰：「惟岳小子驕貴，不達人事，輒拒朝命。

translations.literal: Tao, knowing Xiaozhong was a veteran general skilled in battle with eight thousand elite troops at Yizhou, feared that once campaigning began Xiaozhong would strike from the rear; he therefore sent his aide Cai Xiong to persuade Xiaozhong, saying: "Weiyue is a young man grown proud and high-born, ignorant of human affairs, who rashly defies the court's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Tao, knowing Xiaozhong was a seasoned general skilled in battle with eight thousand elite troops at Yizhou, feared that once the campaign began Xiaozhong would strike from the rear; he therefore sent his aide Cai Xiong to persuade Xiaozhong, saying, "Weiyue is a young man grown proud and high-born, ignorant of the ways of the world, who rashly defies the court's orders.

sentences.zh: 滔奉命伐罪，使君何用助逆，不自求多福耶！

translations.literal: Tao is ordered to punish the guilty—why should you aid the rebel and not seek your own good fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Tao has been ordered to punish the guilty—why should you aid the rebel instead of seeking your own good fortune!

sentences.zh: 今昭義、河東攻破田悅，淮西李僕射收下襄陽，梁崇義投井而卒，臨漢江而誅者五千人，即河南軍計日北首，趙、魏滅亡可見也。

translations.literal: Now Zhaoyi and Hedong have broken Tian Yue; Vice Director Li of Huainan has taken Xiangyang; Liang Chongyi threw himself into a well and died; five thousand were executed beside the Han River; the Henan armies will within days turn north—the destruction of Zhao and Wei is plain to see.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi and Hedong have already broken Tian Yue; Vice Director Li of Huainan has taken Xiangyang; Liang Chongyi threw himself into a well and died; five thousand were executed beside the Han River; the Henan armies will within days turn north—the fall of Zhao and Wei is already in sight.

sentences.zh: 使君誠能去逆効順，必受重任，有先歸國之功矣。」

translations.literal: If you truly cast off rebellion and submit in loyalty, you will surely receive heavy responsibility and the credit of being first to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly cast off rebellion and submit in loyalty, you will surely receive heavy responsibility and the credit of being first to return to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 孝忠然之，乃遣衙官隨雄報滔，又遣易州錄事參軍董稹入朝。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong agreed; he then sent a yamen officer to follow Xiong and report to Tao, and also sent Dong Zhen, registrar of Yizhou, to court.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong agreed; he sent a yamen officer with Xiong to report to Tao, and also dispatched Dong Zhen, registrar of Yizhou, to the capital.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，授孝忠檢校工部尚書、恒州刺史、兼御史大夫，充成德軍節度使，便令與滔合兵攻惟岳，仍賜實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Dezong commended this and appointed Xiaozhong Acting Minister of Works, prefect of Hengzhou, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, with appointment as military commissioner of the Chengde Army; he was ordered at once to join Tao in attacking Weiyue, and was granted an actual fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong commended this and appointed Xiaozhong Acting Minister of Works, prefect of Hengzhou, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, with appointment as military commissioner of the Chengde Army; he was ordered at once to join Tao in attacking Weiyue and was granted an actual fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 其弟孝義及孝忠三女已適人在恒州者，悉為惟岳所害。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiaoyi and Xiaozhong's three daughters who had married and were living in Hengzhou were all killed by Weiyue.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiaoyi and Xiaozhong's three married daughters who were living in Hengzhou were all killed by Weiyue.

sentences.zh: 孝忠甚德滔之保薦，以其子茂和聘滔之女，契約甚密，遂合兵破惟岳之師於束鹿，惟岳遁歸恒州。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong was deeply grateful to Tao for recommending him; he betrothed his son Maohe to Tao's daughter, their bond was very close, and they combined forces to break Weiyue's army at Shulu; Weiyue fled back to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong was deeply grateful to Tao for recommending him; he betrothed his son Maohe to Tao's daughter, their alliance grew very close, and together they broke Weiyue's army at Shulu; Weiyue fled back to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 滔請乗勝襲之，孝忠仍引軍西北，還營義豐，滔大駭。

translations.literal: Tao asked to press the victory and strike Weiyue, but Xiaozhong withdrew his army to the northwest and encamped at Yifeng; Tao was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Tao urged a pursuit to crush Weiyue, but Xiaozhong pulled his army northwest and encamped at Yifeng, to Tao's great alarm.

sentences.zh: 孝忠將佐曰：「尚書布赤心於朱司徒，相信至矣。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong's staff officers said: "Minister, you have laid your loyal heart bare before Vice Director Zhu, and your mutual trust is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong's staff officers said, "Minister, you have laid your loyal heart bare before Vice Director Zhu, and your mutual trust is complete.

sentences.zh: 今逆寇已潰，不終其功，竊所未喻。」

translations.literal: Now the rebel band is already routed— not to finish the victory, we privately cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rebel force is already routed— not to finish the victory, we cannot understand.

sentences.zh: 孝忠曰：「本求破賊，賊已破矣。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong said: "I sought only to break the rebels—the rebels are already broken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong said, "I sought only to break the rebels—the rebels are already broken.

sentences.zh: 然恒州宿將尚多，迫之則困獸猶鬬，緩之必翻然改圖。

translations.literal: Yet many veteran officers remain in Hengzhou; drive them hard and a cornered beast still fights; give them time and they will surely change their plans.
translations.idiomatic: Many seasoned officers still hold Hengzhou. Press them too hard and even a cornered beast will fight; give them breathing room and they will turn on their own.

sentences.zh: 又朱滔言大識淺，可以慮始，難與守成。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhu Tao's words show great knowledge but shallow insight—fit to plan beginnings, hard to share in preserving success.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Zhu Tao talks big but sees little—good at starting schemes, poor at finishing them.

sentences.zh: 吾壁義豐，坐待惟岳之殄滅耳。」

translations.literal: I will fortify Yifeng and sit waiting for Weiyue's destruction."
translations.idiomatic: I shall fortify Yifeng and sit waiting for Weiyue's destruction."

sentences.zh: 旣而朱滔屯束鹿，不敢進軍。

translations.literal: Before long Zhu Tao encamped at Shulu and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhu Tao was stuck at Shulu and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 月餘，王武俊果斬惟岳首以獻，如孝忠所料。

translations.literal: After more than a month Wang Wujun indeed beheaded Weiyue and presented his head, as Xiaozhong had predicted.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month Wang Wujun indeed beheaded Weiyue and presented his head, just as Xiaozhong had predicted.

sentences.zh: 後定州刺史楊政義以州降，孝忠遂有易、定之地。

translations.literal: Later Yang Zhengyi, prefect of Dingzhou, surrendered his prefecture; Xiaozhong then held the territories of Yi and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Zhengyi, prefect of Dingzhou, surrendered his prefecture, and Xiaozhong then held Yi and Ding.

sentences.zh: 時旣誅惟岳，分四州各置觀察使，武俊得恒州，康日知得深、趙二州，孝忠得易州。

translations.literal: At that time, with Weiyue already executed, the four prefectures were each given observation commissioners: Wujun received Hengzhou, Kang Rizhi received Shen and Zhao, and Xiaozhong received Yi.
translations.idiomatic: With Weiyue dead, the four prefectures were divided: Wujun took Hengzhou, Kang Rizhi took Shen and Zhao, and Xiaozhong took Yi.

sentences.zh: 以成德軍額在恒州，孝忠旣降政義，朝廷乃於定州置義武軍，以孝忠檢校兵部尚書，為義武軍節度、易定滄等州觀察等使。

translations.literal: Because the Chengde Army title lay at Hengzhou and Xiaozhong had accepted Zhengyi's surrender, the court thereupon established the Yiwu Army at Dingzhou, appointing Xiaozhong Acting Minister of War as military commissioner of Yiwu and observation commissioner of Yi, Ding, Cang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Chengde Army title lay at Hengzhou and Xiaozhong had accepted Zhengyi's surrender, the court established the Yiwu Army at Dingzhou, appointing Xiaozhong Acting Minister of War as military commissioner of Yiwu and observation commissioner of Yi, Ding, Cang, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 及朱滔、王武俊謀叛，將救田悅於魏州，慮孝忠踵後，滔軍將發，復遣蔡雄往說之。

translations.literal: When Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun plotted rebellion and were about to rescue Tian Yue at Weizhou, fearing Xiaozhong from the rear, Tao's army about to march sent Cai Xiong again to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun plotted rebellion and were about to rescue Tian Yue at Weizhou, fearing Xiaozhong from the rear, Tao sent Cai Xiong again to persuade him as his army prepared to march.

sentences.zh: 孝忠曰：「李惟岳背國作逆，孝忠歸國，今為忠臣。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong said: "Li Weiyue rebelled against the state; Xiaozhong returned to the state and is now a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong said, "Li Weiyue rebelled against the state; Xiaozhong returned to the dynasty and is now a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 孝忠性直，業已効忠，不復助逆矣。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong's nature is straightforward; having already served loyally, I will not aid rebellion again.
translations.idiomatic: I am a plain-spoken man. Having already turned loyal, I will not aid rebels again.

sentences.zh: 往與武俊同行，且孝忠與武俊俱出蕃部，少長相狎，深知其心僻，能翻覆，語司徒，當記鄙言，忽有蹉跌，始相憶也！」

translations.literal: In the past I marched with Wujun, and Xiaozhong and Wujun both came from tribal backgrounds, close from youth; I know well his crooked heart and capacity for reversal—tell the Vice Director to remember my humble words: when a stumble comes, then you will recall them!
translations.idiomatic: In the past I marched with Wujun, and Xiaozhong and Wujun both came from tribal backgrounds and have been close since youth; I know well his crooked heart and his capacity for reversal—tell the Vice Director to remember my humble words: when a stumble comes, then you will recall them!

sentences.zh: 滔又啗以金帛，終拒而不從。

translations.literal: Tao also tried to entice him with gold and silk; he ultimately refused and would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Tao also tried to entice him with gold and silk, but he ultimately refused.

sentences.zh: 易定居二兇之間，四面受敵，孝忠修峻溝壘，感勵將士，竟不受二兇之熒惑，議者多之。

translations.literal: Yiding lay between two villains, attacked on four sides; Xiaozhong built steep ditches and ramparts, roused and encouraged his troops, and in the end was not swayed by the two villains' enticements; many commentators praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yiding lay between two rebel leaders and was threatened on every side; Xiaozhong built steep ditches and ramparts, roused and encouraged his troops, and in the end was not swayed by their enticements; many commentators praised him.

sentences.zh: 又加檢校左僕射，實封至三百戶。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Acting Left Vice Director, and his actual fief reached three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The court further promoted him to Acting Left Vice Director and raised his substantive fief to three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後孝忠為朱滔侵逼，詔神策兵馬使李晟、中官竇文場率師援之。

translations.literal: Later, when Xiaozhong was pressed by Zhu Tao's invasion, an edict ordered Shence Army commissioner Li Sheng and the eunuch Dou Wenchang to lead troops to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xiaozhong was pressed by Zhu Tao's invasion, an edict ordered Shence Army commissioner Li Sheng and the eunuch Dou Wenchang to lead troops to his relief.

sentences.zh: 孝忠以女妻晟子憑，與晟戮力同心，整訓士衆，竟全易定，賊不敢深入。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong gave his daughter in marriage to Sheng's son Ping; he and Sheng exerted themselves with one heart, trained and disciplined the troops, and in the end fully preserved Yi and Ding; the rebels did not dare penetrate deep.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong gave his daughter in marriage to Sheng's son Ping; he and Sheng worked with one heart, trained and disciplined the troops, and in the end fully preserved Yi and Ding; the rebels did not dare penetrate deep.

sentences.zh: 及上幸奉天，令大將楊榮國提銳卒六百從晟入關赴難，收京城，榮國有功。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Fengtian, he ordered Major General Yang Rongguo to lead six hundred crack troops to follow Sheng through the pass to the throne's rescue and recover the capital; Rongguo had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Fengtian, he ordered Major General Yang Rongguo to lead six hundred crack troops to follow Sheng through the pass to the throne's rescue and recover the capital; Rongguo distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 興元元年正月，詔以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xingyuan, an edict made him co-chief minister at his existing rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first Xingyuan year an edict named him Grand Councilor while retaining his existing offices.

sentences.zh: 滄州本隷成德軍，旣移隷義武，其刺史李固烈者，惟岳妻兄也，請還恒州。

translations.literal: Cangzhou had originally been subordinate to the Chengde Army; after it was transferred to Yiwu, its prefect Li Gulei, who was Weiyue's wife's elder brother, asked to return to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhou had once belonged to the Chengde command. After it passed to Yiwu, its prefect Li Gulei—Weiyue's brother-in-law—asked to return to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，孝忠遣牙將程華往滄州交檢府藏。

translations.literal: That year Xiaozhong sent his yamen general Cheng Hua to Cangzhou to take over and inspect the treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xiaozhong dispatched his yamen general Cheng Hua to Cangzhou to take formal receipt of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 固烈輜車數十乗上路，滄州軍士呼曰：「士皆菜色，刺史不垂賑卹，乃稛載而歸，官物不可得也！」

translations.literal: Gulei loaded dozens of supply carts and set out on the road; the soldiers of Cangzhou cried out: "The troops are all gaunt with hunger, yet the prefect will not grant relief—instead he loads up and departs; the official goods cannot be taken!
translations.idiomatic: Gulei loaded dozens of supply carts and set out on the road; the soldiers of Cangzhou cried out, "The troops are all gaunt with hunger, yet the prefect will not grant relief—instead he loads up and leaves; the official goods cannot be taken!

sentences.zh: 殺固烈而剽之。

translations.literal: They killed Gulei and looted him.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Gulei and plundered his goods.

sentences.zh: 程華聞亂，由竇而遁，將士追之，謂曰：「固烈貪暴，已誅之矣，押牙且知州務。」

translations.literal: Cheng Hua heard the turmoil, escaped through a breach in the wall, and was pursued by the troops; they said to him: "Gulei was greedy and violent and has already been executed; you, as yamen aide, shall for now manage the prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hua heard the turmoil, escaped through a breach in the wall, and was pursued by the troops; they told him, "Gulei was greedy and violent and has already been executed; you, as yamen aide, shall for now manage the prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 孝忠即令攝刺史事。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong immediately had him act as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong at once appointed him acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 及朱滔、王武俊稱偽國，華與孝忠阻絕，不能相援。

translations.literal: When Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun declared false states, Hua and Xiaozhong were cut off from each other and could not aid one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun declared rebel states, Hua and Xiaozhong were cut off from each other and could not aid one another.

sentences.zh: 華嬰城拒賊，一州獲全，朝廷嘉之，乃拜華滄州刺史、御史中丞，充橫海軍使，仍改名日華，令每歲以滄州稅錢十二萬貫供義武軍。

translations.literal: Hua closed the city and resisted the rebels; the whole prefecture was preserved; the court commended this and appointed Hua prefect of Cangzhou and Vice Censor-in-Chief, with appointment as commissioner of the Trans-Hai Army; he was also renamed Rihua, and ordered to supply the Yiwu Army each year with one hundred twenty thousand strings of Cangzhou tax money.
translations.idiomatic: Hua closed the city and resisted the rebels, preserving the whole prefecture; the court commended this and appointed him prefect of Cangzhou and Vice Censor-in-Chief, with appointment as commissioner of the Trans-Hai Army; he was also renamed Rihua and ordered to supply the Yiwu Army each year with one hundred twenty thousand strings of Cangzhou tax money.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，河北蝗旱，米斗一千五百文，復大兵之後，民無蓄積，餓殍相枕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, locusts and drought struck Hebei; rice cost one thousand five hundred cash per dou; coming after great warfare, the people had no reserves, and the starving dead lay one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan, locusts and drought struck Hebei; rice cost one thousand five hundred cash per dou; coming after years of war, the people had no reserves, and the starving dead lay one upon another.

sentences.zh: 孝忠所食，豆而已，其下皆甘粗糲，人皆服其勤儉，孝忠為一時之賢將也。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong ate only beans; his subordinates all willingly ate coarse fare; everyone admired his diligence and frugality—Xiaozhong was an exemplary general of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong himself ate nothing but beans, and his men willingly shared the coarsest fare. All admired his thrift—he was counted among the finest generals of the age.

sentences.zh: 三年，加檢校司空，仍以其子茂宗尚義章公主。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Acting Grand Marshal, and his son Maozong was married to Princess Yizhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Acting Grand Marshal, and his son Maozong married Princess Yizhang.

sentences.zh: 孝忠遣其妻鄧國夫人昧谷氏入朝，執親迎之禮，上嘉之，賞賚隆厚。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong sent his wife, Lady of Dengguo of the Megu clan, to court to perform the rites of receiving the bride in person; the emperor commended this and rewarded them with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong sent his wife, the Lady of Dengguo of the Megu clan, to court to perform the bride-receiving rites in person. The emperor praised this and lavished rewards upon them.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，為將佐所惑，以兵入蔚州；

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year, misled by his staff officers, he entered Weizhou with troops;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year his staff misled him into marching troops into Weizhou;

sentences.zh: 尋詔歸鎮，仍以擅興削檢校司空。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered him back to his post, but he was still stripped of Acting Grand Marshal for unauthorized campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon recalled him to his post, but he was stripped of Acting Grand Marshal for campaigning without authorization.

sentences.zh: 七年三月卒，時年六十二，廢朝三日，追封上谷郡王，贈太傅，再贈魏州大都督，冊贈太師，謚曰貞武。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year he died, aged sixty-two; court was suspended three days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shangu Commandery, granted Grand Tutor, then again granted Grand Protector of Weizhou, enfeoffed by patent as Grand Preceptor, with posthumous name Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year he died, aged sixty-two; court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shangu Commandery, granted Grand Tutor, then again granted Grand Protector of Weizhou, enfeoffed by patent as Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous name Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 子茂昭、茂宗、茂和。

translations.literal: His sons were Maozhao, Maozong, and Maohe.
translations.idiomatic: He left three sons: Maozhao, Maozong, and Maohe.

sentences.zh: 子 茂昭茂昭，本名昇云。

translations.literal: His son Maozhao, original name Shengyun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Maozhao, whose original name was Shengyun.

sentences.zh: 幼有志氣，好儒書，以父蔭累官至檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: From youth he had ambition and spirit, loved Confucian books, and by his father's shadow rose in succession to Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had ambition and spirit, loved Confucian books, and by his father's patronage rose in succession to Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年，孝忠卒，德宗以邕王謜為義武軍節度大使、易定觀察使；

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenyuan, when Xiaozhong died, Dezong appointed Prince Yong Yuan as grand military commissioner of Yiwu and observation commissioner of Yi and Ding;
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhong died in the seventh year of Zhenyuan, Dezong named Prince Yong Yuan grand military commissioner of Yiwu and observation commissioner of Yi and Ding;

sentences.zh: 以昇雲為定州刺史，起復左金吾衛大將軍，充節度觀察留後，仍賜名茂昭。

translations.literal: He made Shengyun prefect of Ding, recalled him from mourning as Left Jinwu Guard Major General, appointed him acting observation and military commissioner, and granted him the name Maozhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shengyun was made prefect of Ding, recalled from mourning as Left Jinwu Guard Major General, named acting commissioner, and granted the name Maozhao.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，授節度使，累遷檢校僕射、司空。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he was granted appointment as military commissioner and rose in succession to Acting Vice Director and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he received full appointment as military commissioner and rose through Acting Vice Director to Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 二十年十月，入朝，累陳奏河北及西北邊事，詞情忠切，德宗聳聽，嘆曰：「恨見卿之晚！」

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twentieth year he entered court, repeatedly memorializing on Hebei and northwest frontier affairs with loyal and earnest words; Dezong listened intently and sighed: "I regret meeting you so late!
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twentieth year he entered court and repeatedly memorialized on Hebei and northwest frontier affairs with loyal and earnest words; Dezong listened intently and sighed, "I regret meeting you so late!

sentences.zh: 錫宴於麟德殿，賜良馬、甲第、器用、珍幣甚厚，仍以其第三男克禮尚晉康郡主。

translations.literal: He was granted a banquet in the Qinde Hall and given fine horses, a mansion, utensils, and precious gifts in great abundance; his third son Keli was also married to the Princess of Jinkang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The court feasted him in the Qinde Hall and gave him fine horses, a mansion, utensils, and rich gifts; his third son Keli was married to the Princess of Jinkang.

sentences.zh: 德宗方欲委之以邊任，明年晏駕，茂昭入臨於太極殿，每朝晡預列，聲哀氣咽，人皆獎其忠懇。

translations.literal: Dezong was just about to entrust him with frontier duty when the next year he died; Maozhao attended mourning at the Taiji Hall, taking his place each dawn and dusk in the procession, his voice choked with grief; everyone praised his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was on the point of giving him a frontier command when he died the following year. Maozhao mourned at the Taiji Hall, standing in the dawn and dusk processions with voice broken by grief, and all praised his devotion.

sentences.zh: 順宗聽政，加中書門下平章事，且令還鎮，賜女樂二人，三表辭讓，及中使押犢車至第，茂昭立謂中使曰：「女樂出自禁中，非臣下所宜目睹。

translations.literal: When Shunzong assumed rule, Maozhao was added as co-chief minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery and ordered to return to his post; he was granted two female musicians; thrice he memorialized to decline; when the palace envoy escorted the calf cart to his residence, Maozhao stood and said to the envoy: "Female musicians come from within the forbidden palace—not something a subject should gaze upon.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong assumed rule, Maozhao was added as co-chief minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery and ordered to return to his post; he was granted two female musicians; thrice he memorialized to decline; when the palace envoy escorted the calf cart to his residence, Maozhao stood and said to the envoy, "Female musicians come from within the forbidden palace—not something a subject should gaze upon.

sentences.zh: 昔汾陽、咸寧、西平、北平嘗受此賜，不讓為宜。

translations.literal: Formerly Fenyang, Xianning, Xiping, and Beiping received this gift—it was fitting not to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Prince of Fenyang, the Prince of Xianning, the Prince of Xiping, and the Prince of Beiping received this gift—it was fitting that they did not decline.

sentences.zh: 茂昭無四賢之功，述職入覲，人臣常禮，奈何當此寵賜！
