translations.literal: Maozhao lacks the merit of those four worthies; reporting duty and entering court is a subject's ordinary ritual—how can I accept such favored gifts!
translations.idiomatic: I lack the merit of those four great ministers. Reporting to court is a subject's ordinary duty—how can I accept such extraordinary favor!

sentences.zh: 後有立功之臣，陛下何以加賞？」

translations.literal: Later, when meritorious ministers appear, how will Your Majesty add to their rewards?
translations.idiomatic: When other ministers later win merit, what reward will Your Majesty have left to give them?

sentences.zh: 順宗聞之，深加禮異，允其所讓。

translations.literal: Shunzong on hearing this greatly honored him with special ceremony and granted his request to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong heard this and treated him with exceptional honor, granting his refusal.

sentences.zh: 又錫安仁里第，亦固讓不受。

translations.literal: Again he was granted a residence in Anren Ward, yet again steadfastly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was again offered a mansion in Anren Ward, but once more steadfastly refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，又請入覲，五上章懇切，憲宗許之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, he again requested to enter court for an audience, five times submitting memorials with earnest pleading; Emperor Xianzong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhe he again petitioned to come to court, submitting five earnest memorials until Emperor Xianzong consented.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，至京師，留數月，詔令歸鎮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he arrived at the capital, remained several months, and was ordered by edict to return to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he reached the capital, stayed several months, and was then ordered by edict to return to his post.

sentences.zh: 茂昭願奉朝請於闕下，不許，加太子太保，復令還鎮。

translations.literal: Maozhao wished to serve as a court attendee below the palace gates; this was not permitted; he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and again ordered to return to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhao asked to remain at court as an attendant, but was refused; instead he was made Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince and once again sent back to his command.

sentences.zh: 四年，王承宗叛，詔河東、河中、振武三鎮之師，合義武軍，為恒州北道招討。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wang Chengzong rebelled; an edict ordered the armies of the three commands of Hedong, Hezhong, and Zhenwu, together with the Yiwu Army, to serve as northern-route pacification commissioners against Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Wang Chengzong rebelled, and the court ordered the forces of Hedong, Hezhong, and Zhenwu, together with the Yiwu Army, to form the Northern Route Pacification force against Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 茂昭創廩廄，開道路，以待西軍。

translations.literal: Maozhao established granaries and stables, opened roads, and awaited the armies from the west.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhao built granaries and stables, cleared roads, and prepared to receive the western armies.

sentences.zh: 屬正月望夜，軍吏請曰：「舊例，上元前後三夜，不止行人，不閉里門；

translations.literal: It happened to be the fifteenth night of the first month; military officers requested, saying: "According to old custom, for the three nights before and after the Lantern Festival, travelers are not stopped and ward gates are not closed;
translations.idiomatic: It happened to be the full moon of the first month when military officers petitioned: "By longstanding custom, for the three nights around the Lantern Festival travelers are not halted and neighborhood gates stay open;

sentences.zh: 今外道軍戎方集，請如軍令。」

translations.literal: Now armies on the outer circuits are just assembling; we ask to follow military regulations.
translations.idiomatic: but outer-circuit troops are now gathering here—we ask that military regulations be enforced instead.

sentences.zh: 茂昭曰：「三鎮兵馬，官軍也，安得言外道！

translations.literal: Maozhao said: "The troops and horses of the three commands are imperial armies—how can you call them outer-circuit forces!
translations.idiomatic: Maozhao replied: "The forces of the three commands are imperial troops—how can you speak of them as outsiders!

sentences.zh: 放燈一如常歲。」

translations.literal: Release the lanterns just as in an ordinary year.
translations.idiomatic: Release the lanterns as in any other year.

sentences.zh: 使長男克讓與諸軍分道並進。

translations.literal: He sent his eldest son Kerang to advance by separate routes together with the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched his eldest son Kerang to lead the armies forward along separate routes.

sentences.zh: 克讓渡木刀溝，與賊接戰屢勝。

translations.literal: Kerang crossed the Mudao Gully, joined battle with the rebels, and repeatedly won.
translations.idiomatic: Kerang crossed Mudao Gully and fought the rebels again and again, winning each engagement.

sentences.zh: 茂昭親擐甲冑，為諸軍前鋒，累獻戎捷，幾覆承宗。

translations.literal: Maozhao personally donned armor, served as vanguard for the armies, repeatedly reported victories, and nearly overthrew Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhao himself donned armor and led the vanguard, reporting victory after victory until he nearly brought Chengzong down.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷洗雪承宗，乃詔班師，加檢校太尉，兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: Just then the court cleared Chengzong of charges, and then ordered withdrawal of the army; Maozhao was promoted to acting Grand Commandant and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the court reconciled with Chengzong and ordered the armies withdrawn; Maozhao was promoted to acting Grand Commandant and made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 自安、史之亂，兩河藩帥多阻命自固，父死子代；

translations.literal: Since the An-Shi Rebellion, many military commissioners of the Two He Rivers defied orders to secure themselves, with sons succeeding fathers in command;
translations.idiomatic: Since the An Lushan–Shi Siming Rebellion, most military governors north of the Yellow River had defied the throne to hold their domains, passing command from father to son;

sentences.zh: 唯茂昭表請舉族還朝，隣藩累遣遊客間說，茂昭志意堅決，拜表求代者數四。

translations.literal: Only Maozhao memorialized requesting that his whole clan return to court; neighboring commands repeatedly sent traveling envoys to persuade him covertly, but Maozhao's resolve was firm, and he submitted memorials requesting replacement four times.
translations.idiomatic: only Maozhao petitioned to bring his entire clan back to court. Neighboring commands sent envoys again and again to dissuade him, but his purpose never wavered, and he submitted four memorials asking to be replaced.

sentences.zh: 上乃命左庶子任迪簡為其行軍司馬，乗驛赴之。

translations.literal: The emperor then appointed Left Sub-director of the Crown Prince's Household Ren Dijian as his campaign deputy, who traveled post-haste to join him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then named Ren Dijian, Left Sub-director of the Crown Prince's Household, as his campaign deputy, and Dijian rode post-haste to join him.

sentences.zh: 以兩郡之簿書、管鑰、符印付迪簡，遣其妻季氏、男克讓克恭等先就路，將行，誡之曰：「吾使爾曹侍親出易者，庶後之子孫不為風俗所染，則吾無恨矣。」

translations.literal: He handed over the ledgers, keys, seals, and tallies of the two prefectures to Dijian, sent his wife Lady Ji, sons Kerang and Kegong, and others ahead on the road; when about to depart, he admonished them, saying: "I make you all accompany your elders out of Yi so that, hopefully, later generations of descendants will not be tainted by local customs—then I shall have no regrets.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted Dijian with the ledgers, keys, seals, and tallies of the two prefectures, sent his wife Lady Ji and his sons Kerang and Kegong ahead on the road, and as they were about to leave admonished them: "I am sending you to accompany your elders out of Yi in the hope that future generations will not be corrupted by frontier ways—then I shall die without regret.

sentences.zh: 時五年冬也。

translations.literal: This was in the winter of the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in the winter of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 行及晉州，拜檢校太尉、兼中書令，充河中晉絳慈隰等州節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: When he reached Jin Prefecture, he was appointed acting Grand Commandant and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, and made military governor and surveillance commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Jin Prefecture he was appointed acting Grand Commandant and Director of the Secretariat, and made military governor and surveillance commissioner over Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, and the other prefectures of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 十二月十二日，至京師。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the twelfth month, he arrived at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the twelfth month he reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 故事雙日不坐，是日特開延英殿對茂昭，五刻乃罷。

translations.literal: By precedent the emperor did not hold court on even-numbered days; on this day the Yanying Hall was specially opened to receive Maozhao, and the audience lasted until the fifth watch before ending.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the emperor did not hold audience on even-numbered days, but on this occasion he specially opened Yanying Hall to receive Maozhao; the session lasted five watches.

sentences.zh: 又上表請遷祖考之骨墓于京兆。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial requesting the transfer of the bones and tombs of his ancestors and father to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to have the remains and tombs of his ancestors and father reinterred in the Jingzhao district.

sentences.zh: 在朝兩月，未之鎮。

translations.literal: He remained at court two months and had not yet gone to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed at court for two months and never took up his new post.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，疽發於首，卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, a carbuncle broke out on his head and he died, aged fifty at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year a carbuncle erupted on his head and he died at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 廢朝五日，冊贈太師，賻絹三千匹、布一千端、米粟三千石，喪事所須官給，詔京兆尹監護，謚曰獻武。

translations.literal: Court was suspended for five days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor; condolence gifts were three thousand bolts of silk, one thousand bolts of cloth, and three thousand shi of grain; all funeral needs were supplied by the government; the Jingzhao intendant was ordered to supervise the funeral; his posthumous title was Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning lasted five days. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor, with condolence gifts of three thousand bolts of silk, one thousand bolts of cloth, and three thousand shi of grain; all funeral expenses were met by the state, the Jingzhao intendant was ordered to oversee the rites, and he was given the posthumous title Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 憲宗念其忠藎，諸昆仲子姪皆居職秩，仍詔每年給絹二千匹，春秋分給。

translations.literal: Xianzong, mindful of his loyal devotion, appointed all his brothers and nephews to official ranks, and furthermore decreed an annual grant of two thousand bolts of silk, distributed in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of his loyal service, Xianzong placed all his brothers and nephews in official posts and decreed an annual grant of two thousand bolts of silk, paid in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 克讓、克恭官至諸衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Kerang and Kegong reached the rank of grand generals of the various guard regiments.
translations.idiomatic: Kerang and Kegong rose to the rank of grand generals in the palace guard regiments.

sentences.zh: 小男克勤，長慶中左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The youngest son Keqin, during Changqing, was Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son, Keqin, served during the Changqing era as Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 時有赦文許一子五品官，克勤以子幼，請準近例迴授外甥。

translations.literal: At the time an amnesty edict permitted one son to receive a fifth-rank office; Keqin, because his son was young, requested according to recent precedent to transfer the grant to a nephew.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty edict at the time allowed one son to receive a fifth-rank office; because Keqin's son was still young, he asked, following recent precedent, to redirect the grant to a nephew.

sentences.zh: 狀至中書，下吏部員外郎判廢置，裴夷直斷曰：「一子官，恩在念功，貴於延賞；

translations.literal: When the petition reached the Secretariat, it was sent down to the vice director of the Ministry of Personnel for disposition; Pei Yizhi decided, saying: "The grant of an office to one son is an act of grace recalling meritorious service, valuing the reward of extended honor;
translations.idiomatic: When the petition reached the Secretariat it was referred to the vice director of the Ministry of Personnel for a ruling. Pei Yizhi decided: "The grant of office to one son is grace that honors past merit and extends reward to one's line;

sentences.zh: 若無己子，許及宗男。

translations.literal: If one has no son of one's own, it may extend to male relatives of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: Only when one has no son of one's own may it pass to a male relative of the clan.

sentences.zh: 今張克勤自有息男，妄以外甥奏請，移於他族，知是何人，儻涉賣官，實為亂法。

translations.literal: Now Zhang Keqin himself has a living son; to groundlessly petition with a nephew, transferring it to another clan—who knows who that person might be; if it touches on selling offices, it truly subverts the law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Keqin already has a living son, yet he groundlessly petitions on behalf of a nephew, shifting the benefit to another clan. Who can say who that person really is? If this opens the door to selling offices, it would truly corrupt the law.

sentences.zh: 雖援近日勑例，難破著定格文，國章旣在必行，宅相恐難虛授。

translations.literal: Although recent edict precedents are cited, it is hard to overturn established statutory text; since the national regulations must be enforced, the nephew's ministerial grant can hardly be conferred frivolously.
translations.idiomatic: Recent edict precedents cannot override fixed statutory text. National regulations must be enforced, and a nephew's grant of office cannot be handed out lightly.

sentences.zh: 具狀上中書門下，克勤所請，望宜不允。」

translations.literal: Submit the full report to the Secretariat-Chancellery; Keqin's request should, it is hoped, not be approved.
translations.idiomatic: Submit the full report to the Secretariat and Chancellery. Keqin's request should not be approved.

sentences.zh: 遂為定例。

translations.literal: This thereby became a fixed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This ruling then became a fixed precedent.

sentences.zh: 子 茂宗茂宗以父蔭累官至光祿少卿同正。

translations.literal: Son: Maozong. Maozong through his father's patronage accumulated promotions to Vice Director of the Imperial Banquets with regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Maozong. Through his father's patronage Maozong rose by stages to Vice Director of the Imperial Banquets with regular appointment.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，許尚公主，拜銀青光祿大夫、本官駙馬都尉，以公主幼待年。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, he was permitted to marry an imperial princess; he was appointed Silver-Glitter Grand Master for Imperial Banquets and his original office of Commander-in-Chief of the Princess's Household; because the princess was young, they awaited the proper year.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan he was permitted to marry an imperial princess and was appointed Silver-Glitter Grand Master for Imperial Banquets while retaining his post as Commander of the Princess's Household; because the princess was still young, the marriage was deferred until she came of age.

sentences.zh: 十三，屬茂宗母亡，遺表請終嘉禮。

translations.literal: Thirteen years later, when Maozong's mother died, she left a deathbed memorial requesting completion of the wedding rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen years later, when Maozong's mother died, she left a deathbed memorial asking that the wedding rites be completed.

sentences.zh: 德宗念茂昭之勳，即日授雲麾將軍，起復授左衛將軍同正、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Dezong, mindful of Maozhao's merit, that same day appointed him General of Cloud Pennons, and through mourning resumption appointed him Left Guard General with regular appointment and Commander-in-Chief of the Princess's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of Maozhao's service, Dezong that same day appointed him General of Cloud Pennons and, by resumption from mourning, made him Left Guard General with regular appointment and Commander of the Princess's Household.

sentences.zh: 諫官蔣乂等論曰：「自古以來，未聞有駙馬起復而尚公主者。」

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Jiang Yi and others argued: "Since antiquity, one has never heard of an imperial son-in-law leaving mourning early to marry a princess.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials Jiang Yi and others argued: "From antiquity to the present, no imperial son-in-law has ever left mourning early in order to marry a princess.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿所言，古禮也；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What you say is the ancient rite;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "What you say follows the ancient rites;

sentences.zh: 如今人家往往有借吉為婚嫁者，卿何苦固執？」

translations.literal: yet nowadays many households borrow an auspicious day for marriage—why must you be so obstinate?
translations.idiomatic: but nowadays many families borrow an auspicious day to marry during mourning—why be so stubborn?

sentences.zh: 又奏曰：「臣聞近日人家有不甚知禮教者，或女居父母服，家旣貧乏，且無強近至親，即有借吉以就親者。

translations.literal: They again memorialized: "Your subject has heard that recently among households poorly acquainted with ritual instruction, some daughters still in mourning for parents, their families being impoverished and having no powerful close kin, sometimes borrow an auspicious day to contract marriage.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized again: "We have heard that among families poorly versed in ritual lately, some daughters still in mourning for their parents—impoverished households with no powerful kin nearby—sometimes borrow an auspicious day to marry.

sentences.zh: 至於男子借吉婚娶，從古未聞，今忽令駙馬起復成禮，實恐驚駭物聽。

translations.literal: As for a man borrowing auspicious days to marry, from antiquity it has never been heard; now suddenly ordering an imperial son-in-law to leave mourning and complete the rites truly fears shocking public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: As for a man borrowing an auspicious day to marry, nothing of the kind has ever been heard since antiquity. To order an imperial son-in-law to leave mourning and complete the wedding rites would surely shock all who hear of it.

sentences.zh: 況公主年幼，更俟一年出降，時旣未失，且合禮經。」

translations.literal: Moreover the princess is young; to wait one more year for her marriage would neither miss the proper time nor violate the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the princess is still young. To wait one more year would miss no proper season and would accord with the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 太常博士韋彤、裴堪曰：「伏見駙馬都尉張茂宗猶在母喪，聖恩念其亡母遺表所請，許公主出降，仍令茂宗即吉就婚者。

translations.literal: Grand Masters of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wei Tong and Pei Kan said: "We respectfully observe that Commander-in-Chief of the Princess's Household Zhang Maozong is still in mourning for his mother; in imperial grace, mindful of his deceased mother's deathbed request, the princess's marriage was permitted and Maozong was still ordered to marry on an auspicious day immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees of Sacrificial Rites Wei Tong and Pei Kan said: "We observe that Commander of the Princess's Household Zhang Maozong is still in mourning for his mother, yet in grace to his deceased mother's deathbed request the princess's marriage has been permitted and Maozong ordered to leave mourning and marry at once.

sentences.zh: 伏以夫婦之義，人倫大端，所以關雎冠於詩首者，王化所先也。

translations.literal: We respectfully consider that the meaning of husband and wife is the great foundation of human relations; the reason "Guan Ju" crowns the Classic of Poetry is that royal transformation takes it first.
translations.idiomatic: The bond of husband and wife is the great foundation of human relations; that "Guan Ju" opens the Classic of Poetry shows that royal civilization begins here.

sentences.zh: 天屬之親，孝行為本，所以齊斬五服之重者，人道之厚也。

translations.literal: Kinship by heaven's tie takes filial conduct as its root; the reason the qi and zhan mourning of the five grades of garments is weighty is the thickness of humane obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven-given kinship takes filial conduct as its root; the weight of qi and zhan mourning among the five grades of garments shows how deeply humanity binds us.

sentences.zh: 聖人知此二端為訓人之本，不可變也，故制婚禮，上以承宗廟，下以繼後嗣。

translations.literal: The sages knew these two foundations to be the root of instructing people and that they cannot be altered; therefore they established marriage rites, above to carry on the ancestral temple, below to continue the lineage.
translations.idiomatic: The sages knew these two foundations to be the root of moral instruction and beyond alteration; therefore they established marriage rites to serve the ancestral temple above and continue the lineage below.

sentences.zh: 至若墨衰奪情，事緣金革。

translations.literal: As for wearing black mourning while set aside from grief, the matter arises from military campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Dispensation from mourning in wartime, wearing simplified black garments, applies only when arms are taken up.

sentences.zh: 若使茂宗釋衰服而衣冕裳，去堊室而為親迎，雖云輟哀借吉，是亦以凶瀆嘉。

translations.literal: If Maozong should cast off mourning garments and don ceremonial robes, leave the mourning chamber and go to receive his bride in person, though it be called setting aside grief and borrowing an auspicious day, it would still be defiling the auspicious with the inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: If Maozong casts off mourning garments for ceremonial robes, leaves the mourning chamber to receive his bride in person, and though it be called setting grief aside and borrowing an auspicious day, he would still be polluting a joyous rite with inauspicious mourning.

sentences.zh: 伏願抑茂宗亡母之請，顧典章不易之義，待其終制，然後賜婚。」

translations.literal: We respectfully hope you will set aside the request of Maozong's deceased mother, heed the unchanging meaning of the statutes, wait until his mourning is complete, and then grant the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully ask that you set aside the request of Maozong's deceased mother, uphold the unchanging force of the statutes, wait until his mourning is complete, and only then grant the marriage.

sentences.zh: 德宗不納，竟以義章公主降茂宗。

translations.literal: Dezong did not accept this; in the end Princess Yizhang was given in marriage to Maozong.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong would not listen, and in the end Princess Yizhang was given in marriage to Maozong.

sentences.zh: 自是以戚里之親，頗承恩顧。

translations.literal: From then on, as a relative by marriage, he received considerable imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, as a member of the imperial affinal kin, he enjoyed considerable favor at court.

sentences.zh: 元和中，為閑廄使。

translations.literal: During Yuanhe, he served as Commissioner of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era he served as Commissioner of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 國家自貞觀中至於麟德，國馬四十萬匹在河、隴間。

translations.literal: From the Zhenguan era through Linde, the state's horses numbered four hundred thousand head in the He and Long regions.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhenguan era through Linde the state maintained four hundred thousand government horses in the He and Long regions.

sentences.zh: 開元中尚有二十七萬，雜以牛羊雜畜，不啻百萬，置八使四十八監，占隴右、金城、平涼、天水四郡，幅員千里，自長安至隴右，置七馬坊，為會計都領。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan there were still two hundred seventy thousand; mixed with cattle, sheep, and other livestock, the total was no less than one million; eight commissioners and forty-eight stud offices were established, occupying the four prefectures of Longyou, Jincheng, Pingliang, and Tianshui over an area of a thousand li; from Chang'an to Longyou, seven horse pastures were established as the accounting headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era there were still two hundred seventy thousand horses; together with cattle, sheep, and other livestock the herds numbered well over a million. Eight commissioners and forty-eight stud offices were established across Longyou, Jincheng, Pingliang, and Tianshui—an area a thousand li across—and seven horse pastures were set up from Chang'an to Longyou as the central accounting office.

sentences.zh: 岐、隴間善水草及腴田，皆屬七馬坊。

translations.literal: The good pasturelands and fertile fields between Qi and Long all belonged to the seven horse pastures.
translations.idiomatic: The best pasture and the richest farmland between Qi and Long all belonged to the seven horse pastures.

sentences.zh: 至德以後，西戎陷隴右，國馬盡散，監牧使與七馬坊名額盡廢，其地利因歸於閑廄使。

translations.literal: After Zhide, the western tribes captured Longyou; the state's horses were entirely dispersed; the Stud Pasturage Commissioner and the seven horse pastures were abolished in name and fact, and their profitable lands consequently passed to the Commissioner of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide era the western tribes overran Longyou, the state herds were scattered, the Stud Pasturage Commissioner and the seven horse pastures were abolished in name and fact, and their profitable lands passed to the Commissioner of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，鳳翔節度使請以監牧賦給貧民為業，土著相承，十數年矣。

translations.literal: During Baoying, the Fengxiang military governor requested that stud-pasture tax lands be granted to poor people as their livelihood; native residents had held them in succession for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying era the Fengxiang military governor petitioned to grant stud-pasture tax lands to poor people as their livelihood; local residents had held them in succession for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 又有別勑賜諸寺觀凡千餘頃。

translations.literal: There were also separate edicts granting more than a thousand qing to various monasteries and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Separate edicts had also granted more than a thousand qing to various monasteries and temples.

sentences.zh: 及茂宗掌閑廄，與中尉吐突承璀善，遂恃恩舉舊事，並以監牧地租歸閑廄司。

translations.literal: When Maozong took charge of the Imperial Stud and was on good terms with Palace Commander Tuhu Chenghui, he relied on imperial favor to invoke old claims and gathered all stud-pasture land rents into the Imperial Stud office.
translations.idiomatic: When Maozong took charge of the Imperial Stud and cultivated ties with Palace Commander Tuhu Chenghui, he relied on imperial favor to revive old claims and channel all stud-pasture land rents back to the Imperial Stud office.

sentences.zh: 茂宗又奏麟遊縣有岐陽馬坊，按舊圖地方三百四十頃，制下閑廄司檢計。

translations.literal: Maozong further memorialized that Linyou County had the Qiyang Horse Pasture; according to old maps the area was three hundred forty qing; an order was issued to the Imperial Stud office to investigate and calculate.
translations.idiomatic: Maozong further memorialized that Linyou County contained the Qiyang Horse Pasture, which old maps showed as covering three hundred forty qing, and an order was issued to the Imperial Stud office to survey and calculate the land.

sentences.zh: 百姓紛紜論訴，節度使李惟簡具事上聞，詔監察御史孫革往按問之。

translations.literal: The common people disputed in confusion; Military Governor Li Weijian reported the full matter to the throne; the emperor ordered Investigating Censor Sun Ge to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Common people protested in confusion; Military Governor Li Weijian reported the full matter to the throne, and the emperor ordered Investigating Censor Sun Ge to go and investigate.

sentences.zh: 革還奏曰：「天興縣東五百有隋故岐陽馬坊，地在其側，蓋因監為名，與今岐陽所指百姓侵占處不相接，皆有明驗。」

translations.literal: Ge returned and memorialized: "Five hundred li east of Tianxing County is the former Sui dynasty Qiyang Horse Pasture; the land lies beside it, presumably named after the stud office; it does not connect with the Qiyang site now indicated where common people have encroached—all this has clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Ge memorialized: "Five hundred li east of Tianxing County lies the former Sui Qiyang Horse Pasture; the land beside it took its name from the stud office and does not connect with the Qiyang site now claimed where common people have encroached. The evidence is clear on all points.

sentences.zh: 茂宗怒，恃有中助，誣革所奏不實。

translations.literal: Maozong was enraged; relying on backing from the palace commander, he slandered Ge's report as untrue.
translations.idiomatic: Maozong was furious; counting on support from the palace commander, he accused Ge's report of being false.

sentences.zh: 又令侍御史范傳式覆按，乃附茂宗，盡翻前奏，遂奪居人田業，皆屬閑廄，乃罷革官。

translations.literal: He also had Attending Censor Fan Chuanshi reinvestigate; Fan sided with Maozong, completely reversed the earlier report, seized the fields and estates of residents, and assigned them all to the Imperial Stud; Ge was then dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Attending Censor Fan Chuanshi reinvestigate; Fan sided with Maozong, overturned the earlier findings entirely, seized residents' fields and estates for the Imperial Stud, and Ge was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，岐人論訴不已，詔御史按驗明白，乃復以其地還百姓，貶傳式官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, the people of Qi continued disputing endlessly; the emperor ordered censors to verify clearly; the land was then restored to the common people, and Fan Chuanshi was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Changqing era the people of Qi kept protesting without end; censors were ordered to verify the matter clearly, the land was restored to the common people, and Fan Chuanshi was demoted.

sentences.zh: 茂宗俄授左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Maozong was soon appointed Grand General of the Left Golden Guard Regiment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Maozong was named Grand General of the Left Golden Guard Regiment.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，檢校工部尚書，兼兗州刺史、御史大夫，充兗海沂節度等使，加檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing, he was appointed acting Minister of Works, concurrently Prefect of Yanzhou and Censor-in-Chief, and Military Governor of Yan-Hai-Yi; he was further made acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing he was made acting Minister of Works, concurrently Prefect of Yanzhou and Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of Yan, Hai, and Yi; he was further promoted to acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 大和五年，入為左金吾衛大將軍，充左衛使，轉左龍武統軍卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, he entered court as Grand General of the Left Golden Guard Regiment, served as Commissioner of the Left Guard, transferred to Commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe he entered court as Grand General of the Left Golden Guard Regiment, served as Commissioner of the Left Guard, was transferred to Commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard, and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 子 茂和茂和，元和中為左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Son: Maohe. Maohe, during Yuanhe, was General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Maohe. During the Yuanhe era Maohe served as General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 裴度為淮西行營處置，用兵討吳元濟，建牙赴行營，奏用茂和為都押衙。

translations.literal: When Pei Du was put in charge of the Huaixi campaign headquarters to use troops against Wu Yuanji, he established his command flag and went to the field headquarters, memorializing to employ Maohe as chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du was appointed to direct the Huaixi campaign against Wu Yuanji, he raised his command flag and went to the field headquarters, memorializing to appoint Maohe as chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 茂和嘗以膽氣才略自贊於相府，故度奏用之。

translations.literal: Maohe had once praised himself to the chancellery for courage, spirit, talent, and strategy; therefore Du memorialized to use him.
translations.idiomatic: Maohe had once commended himself to the chancellery for courage, spirit, talent, and strategic ability, and so Pei Du memorialized to employ him.

sentences.zh: 茂和慮度無功，淮、蔡不可平，乃辭之以疾。

translations.literal: Maohe feared Du would achieve no success and that Huai and Cai could not be pacified, and so declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Maohe doubted that Pei Du would succeed and that Huai and Cai could be pacified, and declined the appointment on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 度怒甚，奏請斬茂和以勵行者，憲宗曰：「予以其家門忠順，為卿遠貶。」

translations.literal: Du was greatly angered and memorialized requesting Maohe be executed to encourage those on campaign; Xianzong said: "I consider his family's loyal service and will demote him far away for your sake.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du was furious and memorialized asking that Maohe be executed to encourage the army; Xianzong said: "Out of regard for his family's loyal service, I will have him demoted far away for your sake.

sentences.zh: 後復用為諸衛將軍，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was again employed as a general of the guard regiments and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed as a general in the guard regiments and died in office.

sentences.zh: 附 陳楚陳楚者，定州人，茂昭之甥。

translations.literal: Appendix: Chen Chu. Chen Chu was a native of Dingzhou, Maozhao's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Chen Chu. Chen Chu was a native of Dingzhou and Maozhao's nephew.

sentences.zh: 少有武幹，為義勇牙將，事茂昭，每出征伐，必令典精卒。

translations.literal: From youth he had military talent; he was a junior officer of the righteous army; he served Maozhao, and whenever campaigns were launched, Maozhao always put him in charge of elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed military talent. As a junior officer in the righteous army he served Maozhao, and whenever campaigns were launched Maozhao always put him in command of elite troops.

sentences.zh: 隨茂昭入朝，授諸衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Following Maozhao to court, he was appointed grand general of the guard regiments.
translations.idiomatic: When Maozhao went to court, Chen Chu accompanied him and was appointed grand general of the guard regiments.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年，義武軍節度使渾鎬喪師，定州兵亂，乃除楚易定節度，令馳傳赴任。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe, Yiwu Army Military Governor Hun Hao lost his army; Dingzhou troops mutinied; Chu was then appointed military governor of Yiding and ordered to travel post-haste to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe, Yiwu Army Military Governor Hun Hao lost his army and the troops at Dingzhou mutinied; Chu was then appointed military governor of Yiding and ordered to ride post-haste to his post.

sentences.zh: 亂猶未彌，楚夜馳入州城。

translations.literal: The disorder was not yet quelled; Chu rode through the night into the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: The disorder had not yet subsided when Chu rode through the night into the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 楚家世久在定州，軍中部校皆楚之舊卒，人情大悅，軍卒帖然。

translations.literal: Chu's family had long been in Dingzhou; the officers and commanders in the army were all his old soldiers; popular sentiment was greatly pleased, and the troops were thoroughly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's family had long lived in Dingzhou, and the officers and commanders in the army were all his old soldiers; the people were greatly pleased and the troops settled down at once.

sentences.zh: 轉河陽三城懷節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of Heyang, San Cheng, and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Heyang, San Cheng, and Huai.

sentences.zh: 前後亟立戰功，入為龍武統軍。

translations.literal: Before and after he repeatedly achieved military distinction; he entered court as Commander of the Dragon Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He won repeated military honors and later entered court as Commander of the Dragon Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Changqing era.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：朝廷治亂，在法制當否，形勢得失而已。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The order and disorder of the court depend solely on whether institutions and laws are sound and on the gain or loss of strategic advantage.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Whether the court is well governed or in disorder depends only on whether its laws and institutions are sound and on the gain or loss of strategic advantage.

sentences.zh: 秦人叛上，法制失也；

translations.literal: When the people of Qin revolted against their ruler, institutions and laws had failed;
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Qin turned against their ruler, it was because institutions and laws had failed;

sentences.zh: 漢道勃興，形勢得也。

translations.literal: When the Han Way flourished, strategic advantage had been secured.
translations.idiomatic: when the Han dynasty rose in power, it was because strategic advantage had been secured.

sentences.zh: 臣觀開元之政舉，坐制百蠻；

translations.literal: Your subject observes that under the Kaiyuan administration's successful policies, they seated themselves and controlled the hundred barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Your subject observes that under Kaiyuan's successful governance the court sat at ease and kept the hundred barbarian peoples in check;

sentences.zh: 天寶之法衰，遂淪四海。

translations.literal: When Tianbao's laws declined, the realm sank into chaos throughout the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: when Tianbao's laws decayed, the realm sank into chaos across the four seas.

sentences.zh: 玄宗一失其勢，橫流莫救，地分於群盜，身播於九夷。

translations.literal: Once Xuanzong lost his strategic advantage, the flood tide could not be checked; the land was divided among bandit hosts, and his person was cast among the nine barbarian regions.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuanzong lost his strategic advantage, the flood could not be held back: the land was carved up among bandit armies and his person was driven among the nine barbarian regions.

sentences.zh: 河朔二十餘州，竟為盜穴，諸田兇險，不近物情。

translations.literal: More than twenty prefectures north of the Yellow River became in the end thieves' lairs; the Tian clan were vicious and treacherous, far removed from human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty prefectures north of the Yellow River became in the end dens of bandits; the Tian clan were vicious and treacherous, utterly alien to ordinary human feeling.

sentences.zh: 而弘正、孝忠，頗達人臣之節，沂國力善無報，殆天意之好亂惡治歟！

translations.literal: Yet Hongzheng and Xiaozhong fairly understood a minister's integrity; the Lord of Yi's forceful virtue went unrewarded—perhaps heaven truly favors chaos and hates order!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hongzheng and Xiaozhong fairly understood a minister's duty; the Lord of Yi's strenuous virtue went unrewarded—perhaps heaven truly favors chaos and hates good order!

sentences.zh: 茂昭忠梗有禮，明禍福大端，近代之賢侯也。

translations.literal: Maozhao was loyal, upright, and observant of ritual; he understood the great principles of fortune and disaster— a worthy regional lord of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhao was loyal, upright, and courteous; he saw clearly the great turning points of fortune and ruin—a worthy regional lord of recent times.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：田宗不令，禍淫無應。

translations.literal: Praise states: The Tian clan was lacking in virtue; the punishment of excess found no response.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: The Tian clan lacked virtue, yet punishment for excess found no answer.

sentences.zh: 謂天輔仁，胡覆弘正。

translations.literal: If one says heaven aids the humane, why was Hongzheng overturned?
translations.idiomatic: If heaven truly aids the humane, why was Hongzheng destroyed?

sentences.zh: 茂昭知止，終以善勝。

translations.literal: Maozhao knew when to stop; in the end he prevailed through goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhao knew when to stop, and in the end prevailed through goodness.

sentences.zh: 孰生厲階，上失威柄。

translations.literal: Who raised the ladder of calamity? The ruler lost the handle of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Who raised the ladder of calamity? The ruler lost the handle of power.
